01
Before the first verse · Vol. 2, p. 511

Opening of the surah

Vol. 2, p. 511
Surah ar-Ra'd ([Medinan, and it is said:] disputed; it has forty-three verses [revealed after Surah Muhammad]) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة الرعد ( [مدنية، وقيل] مختلف فيها وهي ثلاث وأربعون آية [نزلت بعد سورة محمد] ) بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 13:1 · Vol. 2, pp. 511–512

Verse 1

The verse as the commentary quotes it
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Mim, Ra. Those are the verses of the Book; and that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe (1)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم المر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ (1)
Vol. 2, p. 511
“Those” is a reference to the verses of the surah. And what is meant by “the Book” is the surah, i.e. those verses are the verses of the perfect surah, wondrous in its kind; then He said “and that which has been revealed to you” of the whole Qur'an “is the truth,” beyond which there is no more, not this surah alone. And in the manner of this speech is the saying of the woman of Anmar: “They are like the hollow ring [source: al-muf'ara] (2), one cannot tell where its two ends are?” — she means the perfect ones (al-kamala).
تِلْكَ إشارة إلى آيات السورة. والمراد بالكتاب السورة، أى: تلك الآيات آيات السورة الكاملة العجيبة في بابها، ثم قال وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ من القرآن كله هو الْحَقُّ الذي لا مزيد عليه، لا هذه السورة وحدها، وفي أسلوب هذا الكلام قول الأنمارية: هم كالحلقة «2» المفرعة، لا يدرى أين طرفاها؟ تريد الكملة.
Vol. 2, p. 512
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 512
1. (1) . His statement “zahida”: in al-Sihah: a “zahid valley” is one that takes little water, and a “zihad land”: i.e. one that flows only from much rain. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «زهيدة» في الصحاح: واد زهيد قليل الأخذ للماء، وأرض زهاد: أى لا تسيل إلا عن مطر كثير. (ع)
03
Q 13:2–3 · Vol. 2, p. 512

Verses 2 to 3

The verses as the commentary quotes them
God is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see; then He established Himself above the Throne and subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. He arranges the matter; He details the signs, that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord (2) And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers, and from all fruits He made therein two mates; He covers the night with the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect (3)
اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ يُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّكُمْ تُوقِنُونَ (2) وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ وَأَنْهاراً وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ جَعَلَ فِيها زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (3)
Vol. 2, p. 512
“God” is a subject, and “the One who” is its predicate, by the evidence of His saying “And it is He who spread the earth”; and it may also be a description. And His saying “He arranges the matter, He details the signs” is a predicate after a predicate. And what precedes it of the mention of the signs supports it. “raised the heavens without pillars that you can see” is a new sentence, adducing as evidence their seeing them thus. And it is said it is a description of “pillars.” The reading of Ubayy supports it: “tarawnahu.” And it is read: “'umud,” with two dammas. “He arranges the matter”: He arranges the matter of His dominion and lordship; “He details the signs” in His revealed books; “that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord” — of recompense, and that to this Arranger and Detailer you must return. Al-Hasan read: “nudabbir,” with the nun. “made therein two mates” — He created in it of all kinds of fruits two by two when He spread it, then they multiplied after that and diversified. And it is said: by the two mates He meant black and white, sweet and sour, small and large, and the like of the differing varieties. “He covers the night with the day” — He clothes it in its place, so it becomes black and dark after having been white and luminous. And it is read: “yughshshā,” with shaddah.
اللَّهُ مبتدأ. والَّذِي خبره، بدليل قوله وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ ويجوز أن يكون صفة. وقوله يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ يُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ خبر بعد خبر. وينصره ما تقدّمه من ذكر الآيات رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها كلام مستأنف استشهاد برؤيتهم لها كذلك. وقيل هي صفة لعمد. ويعضده قراءة أبىّ. ترونه. وقرئ: عمد، بضمتين يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ يدبر أمر ملكوته وربوبيته يُفَصِّلُ آياته في كتبه المنزلة لَعَلَّكُمْ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّكُمْ تُوقِنُونَ بالجزاء وبأن هذا المدبر والمفصل لا بد لكم من الرجوع إليه. وقرأ الحسن: ندبر، بالنون جَعَلَ فِيها زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ خلق فيها من جميع أنواع الثمرات زوجين زوجين حين مدّها، ثم تكاثرت بعد ذلك وتنوعت. وقيل: أراد بالزوجين: الأسود والأبيض، والحلو والحامض، والصغير والكبير، وما أشبه ذلك من الأصناف المختلفة يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ يلبسه مكانه، فيصير أسود مظلماً بعد ما كان أبيض منيراً. وقرئ: يغشى، بالتشديد.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 512
1. (1) . His statement “zahida”: in al-Sihah: a “zahid valley” is one that takes little water, and a “zihad land”: i.e. one that flows only from much rain. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «زهيدة» في الصحاح: واد زهيد قليل الأخذ للماء، وأرض زهاد: أى لا تسيل إلا عن مطر كثير. (ع)
04
Q 13:4 · Vol. 2, pp. 512–513

Verse 4

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And on the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of grapevines, and crops, and palm trees — clustered and non-clustered — watered with one water; and We make some of them superior to others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason (4)
وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ مِنْ أَعْنابٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوانٍ يُسْقى بِماءٍ واحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها عَلى بَعْضٍ فِي الْأُكُلِ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (4)
Vol. 2, p. 512
“neighboring tracts”: lands of differing kinds, though they are neighboring and adjoining: good beside saline, noble beside meager (1), hard beside soft, and fit for crops but not trees beside another the reverse of it, all being arranged in the genus of earth. And that is evidence of an Able, Willing One, who places His acts in one way rather than another. Likewise the crops, vines, and palms growing in these tracts, differing in genera and species, and they are watered with one water, and you see them diverse in fruit — in shapes, colors, tastes, and scents — surpassing one another in them.
قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ بقاع مختلفة، مع كونها متجاورة متلاصقة: طيبة إلى سبخة، وكريمة إلى زهيدة، «1» وصلبة إلى رخوة، وصالحة للزرع لا للشجر إلى أخرى على عكسها، مع انتظامها جميعاً في جنس الأرضية. وذلك دليل على قادر مريد، موقع لأفعاله على وجه دون وجه. وكذلك الزروع والكروم والنخيل النابتة في هذه القطع، مختلفة الأجناس والأنواع، وهي تسقى بماء واحد، وتراها متغايرة الثمر في الأشكال والألوان والطعوم والروائح، متفاضلة فيها.
Vol. 2, p. 513
And in some codices: “qita'an mutajawirat,” on the basis of “and He made.” It is read: “wa-jannatin,” in the accusative by coordination with “two mates,” or in the genitive upon “all fruits.” It is read: “wa-zar'in wa-nakhilin,” in the genitive by coordination with “grapevines” or “gardens.” And “sinwan” is the plural of “sinw,” which is the palm with two heads whose root is one. It is also read with damma. The kasra is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, the damma is the dialect of Banu Tamim and Qays. “yusqa” with ta' and ya'; “wa-nufaddilu” with nun, and with ya', in the passive and the active both. “fi l-ukul” with damma on the kaf and with sukun.
وفي بعض المصاحف: قطعاً متجاورات على: وجعل. وقرئ: وجنات، بالنصب للعطف على زوجين. أو بالجرّ على كل الثمرات. وقرئ: وزرع ونخيل، بالجرّ عطفاً على أعناب أو جنات والصنوان: جمع صنو، وهي النخلة لها رأسان، وأصلهما واحد. وقرئ بالضم. والكسر: لغة أهل الحجاز، والضم: لغة بنى تميم وقيس يُسْقى بالتاء والياء وَنُفَضِّلُ بالنون. وبالياء على البناء للفاعل والمفعول جميعاً فِي الْأُكُلِ بضم الكاف وسكونها.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 512
1. (1) . His statement “zahida”: in al-Sihah: a “zahid valley” is one that takes little water, and a “zihad land”: i.e. one that flows only from much rain. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «زهيدة» في الصحاح: واد زهيد قليل الأخذ للماء، وأرض زهاد: أى لا تسيل إلا عن مطر كثير. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 513
1. (1) . “They went astray, though the path of error is their goal … they have, from right guidance, shackles and fetters.” “The path of error”: figurative for the vile states they are in. And “al-ghull”: that by which the hand is bound to the neck, and the fetter is for the two feet, and both are figurative for heedlessness and following the opinion of the self. He says: they took the path of desire and left the path of guidance.
1. (1) . ضلوا وإن سبيل الغى مقصدهم
…. لهم عن الرشد أغلال وأقياد سبيل الغى: مجاز عما هم عليه من الأحوال الخبيثة. والغل: ما تشد به اليد إلى العنق والقيد للرجلين «وهما مجاز عن الغفلة واتباع رأى النفس. يقول: سلكوا طريق الهوى وتركوا طريق الهدى.
05
Q 13:5 · Vol. 2, p. 513

Verse 5

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And if you are astonished, then astonishing is their saying: When we are dust, shall we indeed be in a new creation? Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord; and those will have shackles on their necks; and those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally (5)
وَإِنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ أَإِذا كُنَّا تُراباً أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَأُولئِكَ الْأَغْلالُ فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ وَأُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ (5)
Vol. 2, p. 513
“And if you are astonished,” O Muhammad, at their saying in denying the resurrection, then their saying is astonishing, worthy of being wondered at, because whoever is able to originate the great creations enumerated to you and was not wearied by creating them, the repetition is the easiest and lightest thing for Him; so their denial was a marvel among marvels. “When we are …” to the end of their saying: it may be in the position of nominative as a substitute for “their saying,” and it may be accusative by “the saying.” And if it is put in the accusative, [it is] by what His saying “shall we indeed be in a new creation” indicates. “Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord”: those are the perfect ones, persistent in their disbelief. “And those will have shackles on their necks” is a description of obstinacy, like His saying “Indeed We have put shackles on their necks.” And the like: “They have, from guidance, shackles and fetters” (1); or it is part of the threat.
وَإِنْ تَعْجَبْ يا محمد من قولهم في إنكار البعث، فقولهم عجيب حقيق بأن يتعجب منه، لأن من قدر على إنشاء ما عدد عليك من الفطر العظيمة ولم يعي بخلقهنّ، كانت الإعادة أهون شيء عليه وأيسره، فكان إنكارهم أعجوبة من الأعاجيب أَإِذا كُنَّا إلى آخر قولهم: يجوز أن يكون في محل الرفع بدلا من قولهم، وأن يكون منصوباً بالقول. وإذا نصب بما دل عليه قوله أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ. أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ أولئك الكاملون المتمادون في كفرهم وَأُولئِكَ الْأَغْلالُ فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ وصف بالإصرار، كقوله إِنَّا جَعَلْنا فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ أَغْلالًا. ونحوه: لَهُمْ عَنِ الرُّشْدِ أَغْلَالٌ وَأَقْيَادُ «1» أو هو من جملة الوعيد
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 513
1. (1) . “They went astray, though the path of error is their goal … they have, from right guidance, shackles and fetters.” “The path of error”: figurative for the vile states they are in. And “al-ghull”: that by which the hand is bound to the neck, and the fetter is for the two feet, and both are figurative for heedlessness and following the opinion of the self. He says: they took the path of desire and left the path of guidance.
1. (1) . ضلوا وإن سبيل الغى مقصدهم
…. لهم عن الرشد أغلال وأقياد سبيل الغى: مجاز عما هم عليه من الأحوال الخبيثة. والغل: ما تشد به اليد إلى العنق والقيد للرجلين «وهما مجاز عن الغفلة واتباع رأى النفس. يقول: سلكوا طريق الهوى وتركوا طريق الهدى.
06
Q 13:6 · Vol. 2, pp. 513–514

Verse 6

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, and there have already occurred before them exemplary punishments. And indeed your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in penalty (6)
وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلاتُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلى ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ (6)
Vol. 2, p. 513
“the evil before the good”: calamity before well-being, and kindness to them in respite. That is because they asked the Messenger of God ﷺ to bring them the punishment, in mockery of his warning. “and there have already occurred before them the mathulat”: i.e. the punishments of their like among the deniers; so what is wrong with them that they do not take heed of them and so stop mocking? And “mathula”:
بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ بالنقمة قبل العافية، والإحسان إليهم بالإمهال. وذلك أنهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يأتيهم بالعذاب استهزاء منهم بإنذاره وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلاتُ أى عقوبات أمثالهم من المكذبين، فما لهم لم يعتبروا بها فلا يستهزءوا. والمثلة:
Vol. 2, p. 514
punishment, on the pattern of “al-samura.” And “mathula” because of the likeness (1) between the punishment and that for which one is punished, “and the recompense of an evil is an evil like it.” It is said: “amthaltu al-rajul min sahibihi” and “aqsastuhu minhu” [I gave the man retribution against his companion]. And “al-mithal”: retaliation. And “al-mathulat” is read with two dammas, by harmonizing the fa' with the 'ayn. And “al-mathalat,” with fatha on the mim and sukun on the tha', as one says “al-samura” (2). And “al-mathulat,” with damma on the mim and sukun on the tha', a lightening of “al-mathulat” with two dammas. And “al-mathulat” is the plural of “mathula,” like “rukba” and “rukbat” (3). “possessor of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing”: i.e. along with their wronging themselves by sins. Its position is circumstantial, in the sense of “wronging themselves” (4), and there are aspects to it: that He means the evil deeds that are expiated for the one who avoids major sins; or major sins on condition of repentance; or He means by forgiveness covering and respite. It is narrated that when it was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Were it not for God's pardon and overlooking, no one would enjoy life; and were it not for His threat and punishment, everyone would rely [on it]” (5).
العقوبة، بوزن السمرة. والمثلة لما بين «1» العقاب والمعاقب عليه من المماثلة، وَجَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُها ويقال: أمثلت الرجل من صاحبه وأقصصته منه. والمثال: القصاص. وقرئ الْمَثُلاتُ بضمتين لإتباع الفاء العين. والمثلات، بفتح الميم وسكون الثاء، كما يقال: السمرة «2» . والمثلات بضم الميم وسكون الثاء، تخفيف المثلات بضمتين. والمثلات جمع مثلة كركبة وركبات «3» لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلى ظُلْمِهِمْ أى مع ظلمهم أنفسهم بالذنوب. ومحله الحال، بمعنى ظالمين لأنفسهم «4» وفيه أوجه. أن يريد السيئات المكفرة لمجتنب الكبائر. أو الكبائر بشرط التوبة. أو يريد بالمغفرة الستر والإمهال. وروى أنها لما نزلت قال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام «لولا عفو الله وتجاوزه ما هنأ أحد العيش، ولولا وعيده وعقابه لا تكل كل أحد» «5»
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 513
1. (1) . “They went astray, though the path of error is their goal … they have, from right guidance, shackles and fetters.” “The path of error”: figurative for the vile states they are in. And “al-ghull”: that by which the hand is bound to the neck, and the fetter is for the two feet, and both are figurative for heedlessness and following the opinion of the self. He says: they took the path of desire and left the path of guidance.
1. (1) . ضلوا وإن سبيل الغى مقصدهم
…. لهم عن الرشد أغلال وأقياد سبيل الغى: مجاز عما هم عليه من الأحوال الخبيثة. والغل: ما تشد به اليد إلى العنق والقيد للرجلين «وهما مجاز عن الغفلة واتباع رأى النفس. يقول: سلكوا طريق الهوى وتركوا طريق الهدى.
Vol. 2, p. 514
1. (1) . His statement “al-mathula lima bayna”: the wording of al-Nasafi is “and al-mathula is the punishment, because of what is between … etc.” (ʿ)
2. His statement “as one says al-samura”: perhaps “al-samura and al-samurat.” (ʿ)
3. His statement “like rukba and rukbat”: in al-Sihah: al-rukba is well known, and the plural of paucity is rukbat, rukbat and rukbat [the three forms are written identically in the source; they differ in vowelling]. And in its margin from Murtada: i.e. with sukun of the kaf, with its damma and with its fatha, the ra' being with damma in all of them. (ʿ) [.....]
4. Mahmud said: “And the position of ‘despite their wrongdoing’ is circumstantial, in the sense of ‘wronging themselves’ … etc.” Ahmad said: The true aspect is that the promise remain upon its unrestrictedness, except where evidence indicates restriction in the case of other than the monotheist; for his wrongdoing — I mean his polytheism — is not forgiven, and what is other than polytheism, its forgiveness is subject to the [divine] will. And al-Zamakhshari builds upon his creed, whose corruption has been made clear, regarding the impossibility of forgiveness for the person of major sins, even if a monotheist, except by repentance; so he restricts it absolutely and confines what is wide; and God is the Granter of success.
5. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tha'labi from the narration of Hammad ibn Salama from 'Ali ibn Zayd from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: When “And indeed your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness” — the verse — was revealed, the Messenger of God ﷺ said … and he mentioned it.
6. His statement “and He did not make the prophets one law”: i.e. equal; thus in al-Sihah. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «المثلة لما بين» عبارة النسفي «والمثلة العقوبة لما بين
…. الخ. (ع)
2. . قوله «كما يقال السمرة» لعله السمرة والسمرات. (ع)
3. . قوله «كركبة وركبات» في الصحاح الركبة معروفة وجمع القلة ركبات وركبات وركبات. وفي هامشه عن مرتضى: أى بسكون الكاف وضمها وفتحها، والراء مضمومة فيهن. (ع) [.....]
4. . قال محمود: «ومحل على ظلمهم الحال بمعنى ظالمين لأنفسهم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: والوجه الحق بقاء الوعد على إطلاقه إلا حيث دل الدليل على التقييد في غير الموحد، فان ظلمه أعنى شركه لا يغفر وما عدا الشرك فغفرانه في المشيئة. والزمخشري يبنى على عقيدته التي وضح فسادها، في استحالة الغفران لصاحب الكبائر وإن كان موحدا إلا بالتوبة، فيقيد مطلقا، ويحجر واسعا، والله الموفق.
5. . أخرجه ابن أبى حاتم والثعلبي من رواية حماد بن سلمة عن على بن زيد عن سعيد بن المسيب: لما نزلت وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ الآية، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
…. فذكره.
6. . قوله «ولم يجعل الأنبياء شرعا واحدا» أى سواء، كذا في الصحاح. (ع)

Q 13:7 · Vol. 2, pp. 514–515

Verse 7

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And those who disbelieve say: Why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord? You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide (7)
وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هادٍ (7)
Vol. 2, p. 514
“Why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord”: out of obstinacy they did not count the signs sent down upon the Messenger of God ﷺ so they proposed the like of the signs of Moses and Jesus, such as the staff turning into a snake and the raising of the dead. So it was said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: You are only a man sent as a warner and one who frightens them of the evil of the outcome, and an adviser like the other messengers, and you have only to bring that by which it is established that you are a warning messenger, and the soundness of that is attained by any sign whatever; and the signs are all equal in the attainment of the soundness of the call by them, there is no disparity among them; and the One with whom everything is by measure gives each prophet a sign according to what His knowledge of the interests and His determination of them required. “and for every people is a guide” among the prophets, guiding them to the religion and calling them to God by a way of guidance and by a sign with which he was singled out, and He did not make the prophets one law (6) in specific signs. And another aspect: that the meaning is that they
لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ لم يعتدوا بالآيات المنزلة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عناداً، فاقترحوا نحو آيات موسى وعيسى، من انقلاب العصاحية، وإحياء الموتى، فقيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنما أنت رجل أرسالات منذراً ومخوّفاً لهم من سوء العاقبة، وناصحاً كغيرك من الرسل، وما عليك إلا الإتيان بما يصح به أنك رسول منذر، وصحة ذلك حاصلة بأية آية كانت، والآيات كلها سواء في حصول صحة الدعوة بها لا تفاوت بينها، والذي عنده كل شيء بمقدار يعطى كل نبى آية على حسب ما اقتضاه علمه بالمصالح وتقديره لها وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هادٍ من الأنبياء يهديهم إلى الدين، ويدعوهم إلى الله بوجه من الهداية، وبآية خص بها، ولم يجعل الأنبياء شرعاً واحداً «6» في آيات مخصوصة. ووجه آخر: وهو أن يكون المعنى أنهم
Vol. 2, p. 515
disavow that what was revealed to you are signs and are obstinate, so let that not concern you; you are only a warner, and you have only to warn, not to establish belief in their breasts, and you are not able to do so; and for every people is a guide able to guide them by compulsion, and He is God the Exalted. And what He appended of the mention of the signs of His knowledge and His determination of things indicates, by the decree of His wisdom, that His giving each warner signs different from the signs of others is a matter arranged by penetrating knowledge, determined by divine wisdom; and had He known good and benefit in answering their proposals, He would have answered them. As for the second aspect, it indicates by it that whoever has this power and this knowledge is the only one able to guide them, knowing by which way He guides them, and there is no way to that for anyone else.
يجحدون كون ما أنزل عليك آيات ويعاندون، فلا يهمنك ذلك، إنما أنت منذر، فما عليك إلا أن تنذر لا أن تثبت الإيمان في صدورهم، ولست بقادر عليه، ولكل قوم هاد قادر على هدايتهم بالإلجاء، وهو الله تعالى. ولقد دل بما أردفه من ذكر آيات علمه وتقديره الأشياء على قضاء حكمته أن إعطاءه كل منذر آيات خلاف آيات غيره: أمر مدبر بالعلم النافذ مقدّر بالحكمة الربانية، ولو علم في إجابتهم إلى مقترحهم خيراً ومصلحة، لأجابهم إليه. وأما على الوجه الثاني، فقد دل به على أن من هذه قدرته وهذا علمه، هو القادر وحده على هدايتهم، العالم بأى طريق يهديهم، ولا سبيل إلى ذلك لغيره.

Q 13:8–9 · Vol. 2, pp. 515–516

Verses 8 to 9

The verses as the commentary quotes them
God knows what every female carries and what the wombs lessen and what they increase; and everything with Him is by due measure (8) Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted (9)
اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثى وَما تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحامُ وَما تَزْدادُ وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدارٍ (8) عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعالِ (9)
Vol. 2, p. 515
“God knows”: it may be a new sentence, and the meaning may be: He is God — an explanation of “guide” on the last aspect — then it began with “He knows what every female carries.” “ma” in “what she carries,” “what the wombs lessen,” and “what they increase” is either relative or infinitive (masdar). If relative, the meaning: He knows what she carries of offspring, in whatever state it is: male and female, complete and premature (1), beautiful and ugly, tall and short, and other states present and anticipated; and He knows what the wombs lessen: i.e. diminish. One says: “ghada l-ma'” and “ghudtuhu” [the water subsided and I made it subside]. From it is His saying “and the water was made to subside.” “and what they increase”: i.e. take as an increase; you say: “I took my right from him and I took an increase from him of such.” From it is His saying “and they added nine.” One says: “zidtuhu fa-zada bi-nafsihi wa-izdada.” Of what the womb lessens and increases is the number of children, for it contains one and may contain two, three, or four. It is narrated that Sharik was the fourth of four in his mother's womb. And of it is the body of the child, for it may be complete or premature. And of it is the duration of its birth, for it may be less than nine months and more than that, up to two years according to Abu Hanifa, up to four according to al-Shafi'i, up to five according to Malik. It is said that al-Dahhak was born after two years, and Haram ibn Hayyan remained in his mother's womb four years, and for that reason was named Haram. And of it is the blood, for it lessens and increases. And if it is infinitive, the meaning is that He knows the pregnancy of every female, and knows the lessening of the wombs and their increase, none of that being hidden from Him, nor its times and states. It is possible that what is meant is the subsiding of what is in the wombs and its increase, so the verb is attributed to the wombs while it belongs to what is in them, on the basis that both verbs are intransitive; and it is supported by the saying of al-Hasan: al-ghaydudah is that she gives birth at eight months or less than that, and the increase is that she adds
اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ يحتمل أن يكون كلاماً مستأنفاً، وأن يكون المعنى: هو الله، تفسيراً لهاد على الوجه الأخير، ثم ابتدئ فقيل يَعْلَمُ ما تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثى «وما» في ما تَحْمِلُ، وَما تَغِيضُ، وَما تَزْدادُ. إما موصولة، وإما مصدرية. فإن كانت موصولة، فالمعنى: أنه يعلم ما تحمله من الولد على أن حال هو. من ذكورة وأنوثة، وتمام وخداج «1» ، وحسن وقبح، وطول وقصر، وغير ذلك من الأحوال الحاضرة والمترقبة، ويعلم ما تغيضه الأرحام: أى تنقصه. يقال: غاض الماء وغضته أنا. ومنه قوله تعالى وَغِيضَ الْماءُ وما تزداده: أى تأخذه زائداً، تقول: أخذت منه حقي، وازددت منه كذا. ومنه قوله تعالى وَازْدَادُوا تِسْعاً ويقال: زدته فزاد بنفسه وازداد، ومما تنقصه الرحم وتزداده عدد الولد، فإنها تشتمل على واحد، وقد تشتمل على اثنين وثلاثة وأربعة. ويروى أن شريكا كان رابع أربعة في بطن أمه. ومنه جسد الولد، فإنه يكون تاما ومخدجا. ومنه مدة ولادته، فإنها تكون أقل من تسعة أشهر وأزيد عليها إلى سنتين عند أبى حنيفة، وإلى أربع عند الشافعي، وإلى خمس عند مالك. وقيل: إنّ الضحاك ولد لسنتين، وهرم بن حيان بقي في بطن أمّه أربع سنين، ولذلك سمى هرما. ومنه الدم، فإنه يقل ويكثر. وإن كانت مصدرية، فالمعنى أنه يعلم حمل كل أنثى، ويعلم غيض الأرحام وازديادها، لا يخفى عليه شيء من ذلك، ومن أوقاته وأحواله. ويجوز أن يراد غيوض ما في الأرحام وزيادته، فأسند الفعل إلى الأرحام وهو لما فيها، على أنّ الفعلين غير متعدّيين، ويعضده قول الحسن: الغيضوضة أن تضع لثمانية أشهر أو أقل من ذلك، والازدياد أن تزيد
Vol. 2, p. 516
upon nine months. And from him: al-ghayd is that which is a miscarriage, not at completion, and the increase is what is born at term. “bi-miqdar”: by a measure and limit which it neither exceeds nor falls short of, like His saying “Indeed, everything We created by measure.” “The Grand”: the great in station, beside whom everything is lesser; “the Exalted”: the One exalted over everything by His power, or the One too grand for the attributes of creatures and exalted above them.
على تسعة أشهر. وعنه. الغيض الذي يكون سقطاً لغير تمام، والازدياد ما ولد لتمام بِمِقْدارٍ بقدر وحدّ لا يجاوزه ولا ينقص عنه، كقوله إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ. الْكَبِيرُ العظيم الشأن الذي كل شيء دونه الْمُتَعالِ المستعلى على كل شيء بقدرته، أو الذي كبر عن صفات المخلوقين وتعالى عنها.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 515
1. (1) . His statement “and khidaj”: in al-Sihah: “khadajat al-naqa khidajan”: she cast her young before the completion of the days, so she is khaadij and it is khadij; or “akhdajat”: when she brings it forth defective in creation, so it is mukhdaj, and it is mukhdaj [sic; the source repeats the word], end. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله و «خداج» في الصحاح: خدجت الناقة خداجا: ألقت ولدها قبل تمام الأيام، فهي خادج، وهو خديج، أو أخدجت: إذا جاءت به ناقص الخلق، فهو مخدج، وهو مخدج اه. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 516
1. (1) . Mahmud said: “If you say: the proper wording would have been to say: ‘and whoever is hiding by night and whoever is moving about by day’ … etc.” Ahmad said: The requirement of the question al-Zamakhshari raised is that the waw be coordinating one of the two attributes to the other, and the requirement of what he answered is that one of the two described be coordinated to the other; and the verse admits another aspect: that the relative pronoun is omitted and its relative clause remains. And the meaning: and whoever is hiding by night and whoever is moving about by day; and the omission of the coordinated relative pronoun while its clause remains is common, especially as the relative pronoun is repeated three times in the verse, and from it is His saying “and I do not know what will be done with me or with you,” where the origin is: “and not what will be done with you,” otherwise the particle of negation would be intruding in a place not its own, because if the second sentence were estimated as entering into the relative clause of the first by way of the coordinating particle, the prohibition [negation] would have no place; and only the relative pronoun, not the clause, accompanied [the negation] in the first. And from it [the line]: “So whoever of you satirizes the Messenger of God … and praises him and helps him — are equal,” i.e. “and whoever praises him and helps him”; and God knows best.
2. “So I spent the night cutting up the provisions between me and him … by the light of a fire at one time and smoke. And I said to him when he bared his teeth like one laughing … with the hilt of my sword in a [firm] place in my hand: Come; if you pledge to me that you will not betray me … we shall be like those who, O wolf, keep company. Are you a man, O wolf — and treachery — you two were … two brothers who were nursed with milk.” By al-Farazdaq, describing a wolf that came to him in a wilderness, so he spent the night cutting up the provisions and dividing them between himself and it, both of them looking on by the light of a fire at one time and by its smoke at another, an indication of the repeated kindling of it. “Takashshiru”: he bared his teeth like one laughing. “Wa-qa'im sayfi”: i.e. while the hilt of my sword was in a great place in my hand, an indication of eagerness and boldness. “Ta'ala”: i.e. approach me so that we make a pact. It is narrated “ta'ashsha,” i.e. eat the supper; “so if you pledge to me after that and bind yourself that you will not betray me, we shall be like those who keep company, O wolf.” And the meaning of “man” is dual, so the referring pronoun returned to it accordingly. And the vocative is a parenthetical between the relative clause and the relative pronoun. And “a anta”: a reproving question. And the repetition of the vocative in it is also a kind of reproof. And “akhayyayn”: diminutive of “akhawayn.” And “al-laban”: the milk of a woman specifically. He likened the wolf and treachery to twins who grew up together from their infancy, suckled by one mother, an indication of perfect inseparability and affinity. And naming the wolf a “man” (imru') is based on placing it in the position of the rational one, validating addressing it. And he likened them to two brothers of the human kind, as the word “laban” indicates, because affinity in it is more perfect and more evident than in others.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت كان من حق الكلام أن يقال: ومن هو مستخف بالليل ومن هو سارب بالنهار
…. الخ» قال أحمد: فمقتضى السؤال الذي أورده الزمخشري أن تكون الواو عاطفة لإحدى الصفتين على الأخرى، ومقتضى ما أجاب به أن يعطف أحد الموصوفين على الآخر، وتحتمل الآية وجها آخر: وهو أن يكون الموصول محذوفا وصلته باقية. والمعنى: ومن هو مستخف بالليل ومن هو سارب بالنهار، وحذف الموصول المعطوف وبقاء صلته شائع، وخصوصا وقد تكرر الموصول في الآية ثلاثا، ومنه قوله تعالى وَما أَدْرِي ما يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلا بِكُمْ والأصل: ولا ما يفعل بكم، وإلا كان حرف النفي دخيلا في غير موضعه، لأن الجملة الثانية لو قدرت داخلة في صلة الأول بواسطة العاطف لم يكن للنهى موقع، وإنما صحب في الأول الموصول لا الصلة. ومنه: فمن بهجو رسول الله منكم
…. ويمدحه وينصره سواء أى ومن يمدحه وينصره، والله أعلم.
2. . فبت أقد الزاد بيني وبينه
…. على ضوء نار مرة ودخان فقلت له لما تكشر ضاحكا
…. وقائم سيفي من يدي بمكان تعال فان عاهدتني لا تخوننى
…. نكن مثل من يا ذئب يصطحبان أأنت امرؤ يا ذئب والغدر كنتما
…. أخيين كانا أرضعا بلبان للفرزدق، يصف ذئبا أتاه في مفازة فبات يقطع الزاد ويقسمه بينه وبينه، حال كونهما مشرفين على ضوء نار تارة وعلى دخانها أخرى، دلالة على تكرر إيقادها. وتكشر: أبدى أنيابه كالضاحك. وقائم سيفي: أى والحال أن مقبض سيفي بمكان عظيم من يدي، دلالة على الحرص والجرأة. تعال: أى أقبل إلى نتعاهد. ويروى تعش أى كل العشاء، فان عاهدتني بعد ذلك والتزمت أنك لا تخوننى: نكن مثل من يصطحبان يا ذئب. ومعنى «من» مثنى، فعاد عليه الرابط كذلك. والنداء. اعتراض بين الصلة والموصول. وأ أنت: استفهام توبيخي. وتكرير النداء فيه نوع توبيخ أيضا. وأخيين: مصغر أخوين. واللبان: لبن المرأة خاصة. شبه الذئب والغدر بتوأمين نشئا معا من صغرهما ترضعهما أم واحدة، دلالة على كمال التلازم والتآلف. وتسمية الذئب امرأ، مبنية على تنزيله منزلة العاقل المصحح لخطابه. وشبههما بالأخوين من نوع الإنسان، كما دل على ذلك لفظ اللبان، لأن التآلف فيه أكمل وأظهر منه في غيره.
09
Q 13:10–11 · Vol. 2, pp. 516–517

Verses 10 to 11

The verses as the commentary quotes them
It is the same [to Him] whether any of you conceals his speech or publicizes it, and whether he is hidden by night or moving about by day (10) For him are successive angels before him and behind him, who guard him by the command of God. Indeed God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when God intends for a people evil, there is no repelling it, and there is not for them besides Him any protector (11)
سَواءٌ مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَسَرَّ الْقَوْلَ وَمَنْ جَهَرَ بِهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ وَسارِبٌ بِالنَّهارِ (10) لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَإِذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوْءاً فَلا مَرَدَّ لَهُ وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ والٍ (11)
Vol. 2, p. 516
“sarib”: going in his “sarb” — with fatha — i.e. in his path and direction. One says: “saraba fi l-ard suruban.” The meaning: equal with Him is the one who hides, i.e. seeks concealment in a hiding place at night in its darkness, and the one who moves about the roads openly by day, whom everyone sees.
سارِبٌ ذاهب في سربه- بالفتح- أى في طريقه ووجهه. يقال: سرب في الأرض سروبا. والمعنى: سواء عنده من استخفى: أى طلب الخفاء في مختبإ بالليل في ظلمته، ومن يضطرب في الطرقات ظاهراً بالنهار يبصره كل أحد.
Question
If you say: the proper wording would have been: “and whoever is hiding by night and whoever is moving about by day” (1), so that the meaning of equality would take in the hider and the mover; otherwise it takes in one who is both hider and mover.
فإن قلت: كان حق العبارة أن يقال: ومن هو مستخف بالليل ومن هو سارب بالنهار «1» ، حتى يتناول معنى الاستواء المستخفى والسارب، وإلا فقد تناول واحداً هو مستخف وسارب.
Answer
I say: there are two aspects to it: one, that “and one who moves about” is coordinated to “whoever is hiding,” not to “hiding”; the second, that it is coordinated to “hiding,” except that “man” has the meaning of two, as in his saying: “we shall be like the two who, O wolf, keep company” (2)
قلت: فيه وجهان: أحدهما أنّ قوله وَسارِبٌ عطف على من هو مستخف، لا على مستخف، والثاني أنه عطف على مستخف، إلا أن مَنْ في معنى الاثنين، كقوله: نَكُنْ مِثْلَ مَنْ يَاذِئْبُ يصْطَحِبَانِ «2»
Vol. 2, p. 517
as if it were said: Equal among you are two: one hiding by night and one moving about by day. And the pronoun in “lahu” refers back to “man,” as if it were said: for whoever conceals and whoever publicizes, and whoever hides and whoever moves about, “mu'aqqibat”: groups of angels who succeed one another in guarding and protecting him; the origin is “mu'taqibat,” so the ta' was assimilated into the qaf, like His saying “and the excuse-makers came” in the sense of “al-mu'tadhirun.” “Mu'aqqibat” with kasra on the 'ayn is also possible, though not read. Or it is “muf'ilat” from “aqqabahu” when he came upon his heel ('aqib), as one says “qafa',” since some of them follow others. Or because they follow up what he speaks and record it. “They guard him by the command of God”: the two are both descriptions (1), and “min amr God” is not connected with “guarding,” as if it were said: “for him are successive angels from the command of God.” Or “they guard him for the sake of God's command,” i.e. because God commanded them to guard him. The evidence for it is the reading of 'Ali ؓ Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad and 'Ikrima: “yahfazunahu bi-amr God.” Or “they guard him from the might of God and His vengeance when he sins,” through their supplication for him and their asking their Lord to give him respite in hope that he repents and turns back, like His saying “Say: Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?” It is also said: the “mu'aqqibat” are the guards and attendants (2) around the sultan, who guard him in his imagining and estimation from the command of God, i.e. from His decrees and calamities; or this is by way of mockery of him. And it is read “lahu ma'aqib,” the plural of “mu'aqqib” or “mu'aqqiba.” And the ya' is a compensation for the omission of one of the two qafs in the broken plural. “Indeed God does not change what is in a people” of well-being and blessing “until they change what is in themselves” of the good state, by the abundance of disobedience; “min wal”: of anyone who takes charge of their affair and repels it from them.
كأنه قيل: سواء منكم اثنان: مستخف بالليل، وسارب بالنهار. والضمير في لَهُ مردود على مِنْ كأنه قيل: لمن أسرّ ومن جهر، ومن استخفى ومن سرب مُعَقِّباتٌ جماعات من الملائكة تعتقب في حفظه وكلاءته، والأصل: معتقبات، فأدغمت التاء في القاف، كقوله وَجاءَ الْمُعَذِّرُونَ بمعنى المعتذرون. ويجوز معقبات، بكسر العين ولم يقرأ به. أو هو مفعلات من عقبه إذا جاء على عقبه، كما يقال: قفاء، لأنّ بعضهم يعقب بعضاً. أو لأنهم يعقبون ما يتكلم به فيكتبونه يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ هما صفتان جميعاً، «1» وليس مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ بصلة للحفظ، كأنه قيل: له معقبات من أمر الله. أو يحفظونه من أجل أمر الله، أى: من أجل أنّ الله أمرهم بحفظه. والدليل عليه قراءة على رضى الله عنه وابن عباس وزيد بن على وجعفر بن محمد وعكرمة: يحفظونه بأمر الله. أو يحفظونه من بأس الله ونقمته إذا أذنب، بدعائهم له ومسألتهم ربهم أن يمهله رجاء أن يتوب وينيب، كقوله قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمنِ وقيل: المعقبات الحرس والجلاوزة «2» حول السلطان، يحفظونه في توهمه وتقديره من أمر الله أى من قضاياه ونوازله، أو على التهكم به، وقرئ له معاقيب جمع معقب أو معقبة. والياء عوض من حذف إحدى القافين في التكسير إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَوْمٍ من العافية والنعمة حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ من الحال الجميلة بكثرة المعاصي مِنْ والٍ ممن يلي أمرهم ويدفعه عنهم.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 516
1. (1) . Mahmud said: “If you say: the proper wording would have been to say: ‘and whoever is hiding by night and whoever is moving about by day’ … etc.” Ahmad said: The requirement of the question al-Zamakhshari raised is that the waw be coordinating one of the two attributes to the other, and the requirement of what he answered is that one of the two described be coordinated to the other; and the verse admits another aspect: that the relative pronoun is omitted and its relative clause remains. And the meaning: and whoever is hiding by night and whoever is moving about by day; and the omission of the coordinated relative pronoun while its clause remains is common, especially as the relative pronoun is repeated three times in the verse, and from it is His saying “and I do not know what will be done with me or with you,” where the origin is: “and not what will be done with you,” otherwise the particle of negation would be intruding in a place not its own, because if the second sentence were estimated as entering into the relative clause of the first by way of the coordinating particle, the prohibition [negation] would have no place; and only the relative pronoun, not the clause, accompanied [the negation] in the first. And from it [the line]: “So whoever of you satirizes the Messenger of God … and praises him and helps him — are equal,” i.e. “and whoever praises him and helps him”; and God knows best.
2. “So I spent the night cutting up the provisions between me and him … by the light of a fire at one time and smoke. And I said to him when he bared his teeth like one laughing … with the hilt of my sword in a [firm] place in my hand: Come; if you pledge to me that you will not betray me … we shall be like those who, O wolf, keep company. Are you a man, O wolf — and treachery — you two were … two brothers who were nursed with milk.” By al-Farazdaq, describing a wolf that came to him in a wilderness, so he spent the night cutting up the provisions and dividing them between himself and it, both of them looking on by the light of a fire at one time and by its smoke at another, an indication of the repeated kindling of it. “Takashshiru”: he bared his teeth like one laughing. “Wa-qa'im sayfi”: i.e. while the hilt of my sword was in a great place in my hand, an indication of eagerness and boldness. “Ta'ala”: i.e. approach me so that we make a pact. It is narrated “ta'ashsha,” i.e. eat the supper; “so if you pledge to me after that and bind yourself that you will not betray me, we shall be like those who keep company, O wolf.” And the meaning of “man” is dual, so the referring pronoun returned to it accordingly. And the vocative is a parenthetical between the relative clause and the relative pronoun. And “a anta”: a reproving question. And the repetition of the vocative in it is also a kind of reproof. And “akhayyayn”: diminutive of “akhawayn.” And “al-laban”: the milk of a woman specifically. He likened the wolf and treachery to twins who grew up together from their infancy, suckled by one mother, an indication of perfect inseparability and affinity. And naming the wolf a “man” (imru') is based on placing it in the position of the rational one, validating addressing it. And he likened them to two brothers of the human kind, as the word “laban” indicates, because affinity in it is more perfect and more evident than in others.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت كان من حق الكلام أن يقال: ومن هو مستخف بالليل ومن هو سارب بالنهار
…. الخ» قال أحمد: فمقتضى السؤال الذي أورده الزمخشري أن تكون الواو عاطفة لإحدى الصفتين على الأخرى، ومقتضى ما أجاب به أن يعطف أحد الموصوفين على الآخر، وتحتمل الآية وجها آخر: وهو أن يكون الموصول محذوفا وصلته باقية. والمعنى: ومن هو مستخف بالليل ومن هو سارب بالنهار، وحذف الموصول المعطوف وبقاء صلته شائع، وخصوصا وقد تكرر الموصول في الآية ثلاثا، ومنه قوله تعالى وَما أَدْرِي ما يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلا بِكُمْ والأصل: ولا ما يفعل بكم، وإلا كان حرف النفي دخيلا في غير موضعه، لأن الجملة الثانية لو قدرت داخلة في صلة الأول بواسطة العاطف لم يكن للنهى موقع، وإنما صحب في الأول الموصول لا الصلة. ومنه: فمن بهجو رسول الله منكم
…. ويمدحه وينصره سواء أى ومن يمدحه وينصره، والله أعلم.

Vol. 2, p. 517
1. (1) . His speech resumes. He said: “And the meaning of His saying ‘For him are successive angels before him and behind him; they guard him by the command of God’: the two are both descriptions, and ‘min amr God’ is not connected with guarding, as if it were said: for him … etc.” Ahmad said: The reality of this aspect is that they guard him from the thing which God knew that He would repel from him because of their supplication. And were it not for this cause, it would have been in God's knowledge that vengeance would descend upon him, because God Almighty knows what would not be, if it were, how it would be; our Lord encompasses everything in knowledge.
2. His statement “wa-l-jalawiza”: in al-Sihah: “al-jilwaz”: the policeman, and the plural is “jalawiza.” (ʿ)
1. (1) . عاد كلامه. قال: ومعنى قوله لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ هما صفتان جميعا وليس من أمر الله بصلة الحفظ كأنه قيل له
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وحقيقة هذا الوجه أنهم يحفظونه من الأمر الذي علم الله أنه يدفعه عنه بسبب دعائهم. ولولا هذا السبب لكان في علم الله أن النقمة تحل عليه، لأن الله عز وجل يعلم ما لا يكون لو كان كيف كان يكون، وسع ربنا كل شيء علما.
2. . قوله «والجلاوزة» في الصحاح «الجلواز» الشرطي، والجمع الجلاوزة. (ع)

Q 13:12–13 · Vol. 2, pp. 517–520

Verses 12 to 13

The verses as the commentary quotes them
It is He who shows you the lightning, as fear and aspiration, and brings forth the heavy clouds (12) And the thunder exalts with His praise, and the angels from fear of Him; and He sends thunderbolts and strikes therewith whom He wills, while they dispute about God; and He is severe in His stratagem (al-mihal) (13)
هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحابَ الثِّقالَ (12) وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّواعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِها مَنْ يَشاءُ وَهُمْ يُجادِلُونَ فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ الْمِحالِ (13)
Vol. 2, p. 518
“fear and aspiration” cannot be objects of purpose (1), because they are not the act of the agent of the verb being explained, except on the estimation of an omitted annexed noun, i.e. “the intention of fear and aspiration,” or in the sense of “frightening and inspiring aspiration.” It is also possible that they are accusatives as circumstantials from “lightning,” as if it were in itself fear and aspiration; or in the sense of “possessing fear and possessing aspiration”; or [circumstantials] from the addressees, i.e. “fearing and aspiring.” And the meaning of fear and aspiration: that the falling of thunderbolts is feared when the lightning flashes, and rain is aspired to. Abu al-Tayyib said: “A youth like the dark cloud, feared and hoped for … life-giving rain is hoped for from it and thunderbolts are feared” (2). And it is said: the rain is feared by one for whom it is harmful, like the traveler, and one who has dates and raisins on his threshing floor, and one whose house leaks (3); and among lands are those whose people do not benefit from rain, like the people of Egypt; and it is aspired to by one for whom it is beneficial and who lives by it. “al-sahab”: a generic noun, the singular being “sahaba.” And “al-thiqal” is the plural of “thaqila,” because you say “a heavy cloud” and “heavy clouds,” as you say “a noble woman” and “noble women,” and they are the ones heavy with water. “And the thunder exalts with His praise”: and the hearer of the thunder among the servants who hope for rain exalt Him, praising Him, i.e. they clamor with “Glory be to God” and “Praise be to God.” And from the Prophet ﷺ that he used to say: “Glory be to the One whom the thunder exalts with His praise” (4). And from 'Ali ؓ: “Glory be to the One for whom you [thunder] glorify.” And when the thunder intensified, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “O God, do not kill us with Your wrath, nor destroy us with Your punishment, and grant us well-being before that” (5). And from Ibn 'Abbas: the Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ about thunder, what it is? He said: “An angel of
خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً لا يصح أن يكونا مفعولا لهما «1» لأنهما ليسا بفعل فاعل الفعل المعلل إلا على تقدير حذف المضاف، أى: إرادة خوف وطمع. أو على معنى إخافة وإطماعاً. ويجوز أن يكونا منتصبين على الحال من البرق، كأنه في نفسه خوف وطمع. أو على: ذا خوف وذا طمع. أو من المخاطبين، أى: خائفين وطامعين. ومعنى الخوف والطمع: أنّ وقوع الصواعق يخاف عند لمع البرق، ويطمع في الغيث. قال أبو الطيب: فَتى كَالسَّحَابِ الْجُونِ تُخْشَى وَتُرْتَجَى … يُرْجَى الْحَيَا مِنْهَا وَيُخْشَى الصَّوَاعِقُ «2» وقيل: يخاف المطر من له فيه ضرر، كالمسافر، ومن له في جرينه التمر والزبيب، ومن له بيت يكف «3» ، ومن البلاد مالا ينتفع أهله بالمطر كأهل مصر، ويطمع فيه من له فيه نفع، ويحيا به السَّحابَ اسم الجنس، والواحدة سحابة. والثِّقالَ جمع ثقيلة، لأنك تقول سحابة ثقيلة، وسحاب ثقال، كما تقول: امرأة كريمة ونساء كرام، وهي الثقال بالماء وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ ويسبح سامع الرعد من العباد الراجين للمطر حامدين له. أى يضجون بسبحان الله والحمد لله. وعن النبىّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول «سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده» «4» وعن على رضى الله عنه: سبحان من سبحت له. وإذا اشتدّ الرعد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «اللهمّ لا تقتلنا بغضبك، ولا تهلكنا بعذابك، وعافنا قبل ذلك» «5» وعن ابن عباس أنّ اليهود سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الرعد ما هو؟ فقال: «ملك من
Vol. 2, p. 519
the angels in charge of the clouds; with him are twisted cloths (1) of fire with which he drives the clouds” (2). And from al-Hasan: a creature among God's creatures, not an angel. And among the innovations of the Sufis: thunder is the swoonings of the angels, lightning is the sighs of their hearts, and rain is their weeping. “and the angels from fear of Him”: and the angels exalt Him out of awe of Him and magnification of Him. He mentioned His penetrating knowledge in everything and the equality with Him of the manifest and the hidden, and what indicates His dazzling power and His oneness; then He said “and they” — meaning those who disbelieved and denied the Messenger of God and rejected his signs — “dispute about God,” in that they reject what the Messenger describes Him with, of power to resurrect and to restore creatures, by their saying “Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?”, and they reject the oneness by taking partners and equals, and make Him one of the begetting bodies by their saying “the angels are daughters of God.” This is their disputation by falsehood, like their saying “and they disputed by falsehood to refute thereby the truth.” And it is said: the waw is circumstantial, i.e.: He strikes therewith whom He wills in the state of their disputation. That is because Arbad, brother of Labid ibn Rabi'a al-'Amiri, said to the Messenger of God ﷺ when he came to him with 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl, intending to kill him — and God struck 'Amir with a gland like the gland of a camel (3), and death in the house of a woman of Salul, and sent upon Arbad a thunderbolt that killed him — “Tell us of our Lord: is He of brass or of iron?” (4) “al-mihal”: al-mumahala, which is intensity of scheming and plotting. From it: “tamahhala li-kadha” when he exerts himself in using stratagem and strives in it. And “mahala bi-fulan” when he plotted against him and informed on him to the sultan. And from it the hadith: “and do not make it, against us, a disputant who is believed” (5). And al-A'sha said:
الملائكة موكل بالسحاب، معه مخاريق «1» من نار يسوق بها السحاب» «2» وعن الحسن: خلق من خلق الله ليس بملك. ومن بدع المتصوّفة. الرعد صعقات الملائكة، والبرق زفرات أفئدتهم، والمطر بكاؤهم وَالْمَلائِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ ويسبح الملائكة من هيبته وإجلاله. ذكر علمه النافذ في كل شيء واستواء الظاهر والخفي عنده، وما دلّ على قدرته الباهرة ووجدانيته ثم قال وَهُمْ يعنى الذين كفروا وكذّبوا رسول الله وأنكروا آياته يُجادِلُونَ فِي اللَّهِ حيث ينكرون على رسوله ما يصفه به من القدرة على البعث وإعادة الخلائق بقولهم مَنْ يُحْيِ الْعِظامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ ويردّون الواحدانية باتخاذ الشركاء والأنداد، ويجعلونه بعض الأجسام المتوالدة بقولهم «الملائكة بنات الله» فهذا جدالهم بالباطل، كقولهم وَجادَلُوا بِالْباطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الْحَقَّ وقيل: الواو للحال. أى: فيصيب بها من يشاء في حال جدالهم. وذلك أنّ أربد أخا لبيد ابن ربيعة العامري قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين وفد عليه معه عامر بن الطفيل قاصدين لقتله فرمى الله عامراً بغدّة كغدّة البعير «3» وموت في بيت سلولية، وأرسل على أربد صاعقة فقتلته- أخبرنا عن ربنا أمن نحاس هو أم من حديد؟ «4» الْمِحالِ المماحلة، وهي شدّة المماكرة والمكايدة. ومنه: تمحل لكذا، إذا تكلف استعمال الحيلة واجتهد فيه. ومحل بفلان إذا كاده وسعى به إلى السلطان. ومنه الحديث: «ولا تجعله علينا ماحلا «5» مصدّقا» وقال الأعشى:
Vol. 2, p. 520
“A branch of the nab' tree, gentle amid the bough of glory … abundant of dew, severe in stratagem (al-mihal)” (1). And the meaning is that He is severe in scheming and plotting against His enemies, bringing them destruction from where they do not expect. And al-A'raj read “al-mahal” with fatha on the mim, on the basis that it is “maf'al,” from “hala yahulu mahalan” when he schemed. From it: “ahwal min dhi'b” [more cunning than a wolf], i.e. more intense in scheme. It is possible that the meaning is “severe in the vertebrae (al-fiqar) (2),” and it would be a proverb for strength and power, as in “So God's forearm is stronger, and His razor sharper,” because an animal, when its “mihal” is intense, is described as intensely strong and capable of what others are unable to do. Do you not see their saying “fa-qarathu al-fawaqir” [calamities broke his back]? That is because the “fiqar” is the pillar and mainstay of the back.
فَرْعُ نَبْعٍ يَهَشُّ فِى غُصُنِ الْمَجْ … دِ غَزِيرُ النّدَى شَدِيدُ الْمِحَالِ «1» والمعنى أنه شديد المكر والكيد لأعدائه، يأتيهم بالهلكة من حيث. لا يحتسبون. وقرأ الأعرج بفتح الميم، على أنه مفعل، من حال يحول محالا إذا احتال. ومنه: أحول من ذئب، أى أشدّ حيلة. ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: شديد الفقار «2» ، ويكون مثلا في القوة والقدرة كما جاء: فساعد الله أشدّ، وموساه أحدّ، لأن الحيوان إذا اشتدّ محاله، كان منعوتاً بشدّة القوّة والاضطلاع بما يعجز عنه غيره. ألا ترى إلى قولهم: فقرته الفواقر؟ وذلك أن الفقار عمود الظهر وقوامه.
Editor’s notes on these 4 pages
Vol. 2, p. 517
1. (1) . His speech resumes. He said: “And the meaning of His saying ‘For him are successive angels before him and behind him; they guard him by the command of God’: the two are both descriptions, and ‘min amr God’ is not connected with guarding, as if it were said: for him … etc.” Ahmad said: The reality of this aspect is that they guard him from the thing which God knew that He would repel from him because of their supplication. And were it not for this cause, it would have been in God's knowledge that vengeance would descend upon him, because God Almighty knows what would not be, if it were, how it would be; our Lord encompasses everything in knowledge.
2. His statement “wa-l-jalawiza”: in al-Sihah: “al-jilwaz”: the policeman, and the plural is “jalawiza.” (ʿ)
1. (1) . عاد كلامه. قال: ومعنى قوله لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ هما صفتان جميعا وليس من أمر الله بصلة الحفظ كأنه قيل له
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وحقيقة هذا الوجه أنهم يحفظونه من الأمر الذي علم الله أنه يدفعه عنه بسبب دعائهم. ولولا هذا السبب لكان في علم الله أن النقمة تحل عليه، لأن الله عز وجل يعلم ما لا يكون لو كان كيف كان يكون، وسع ربنا كل شيء علما.
2. . قوله «والجلاوزة» في الصحاح «الجلواز» الشرطي، والجمع الجلاوزة. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 518
1. (1) . Mahmud said: “‘fear and aspiration’ cannot be objects of purpose because they are not the act … etc.” Ahmad said: Or [they can be] objects of purpose, on the basis that the object of purpose in a verb such as this is an agent in meaning, because when He shows them, they see; and the origin is: “and He is the One who shows you the lightning so that you see it as fear and aspiration,” i.e. you watch for it and look at it, at one time for the sake of fear and at another for the sake of aspiration; and God knows best.
2. He says: he is a courageous, generous youth, whose evil is feared and whose good is hoped for, so he is like the black cloud. And “al-jawn”: the black; and it is also applied to the white. Ibn Jinni narrated it with damma so as to be a plural, i.e. the black, darkening ones, because cloud is a plural in meaning. “yurtaja al-haya”: i.e. rain, from them. And we fear their thunderbolts, which are the pieces of fire that descend from them.
3. His statement “wa-man lahu bayt yakifu”: “wakafa al-bayt yakifu”: it dripped, as in al-Sihah. (ʿ)
4. Narrated by al-Tabari from the narration of Isra'il from Layth from a man from Abu Hurayra, raised [to the Prophet]: “that when he heard thunder he used to say: Glory be to the One whom the thunder exalts with His praise.” And al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Adab al-Mufrad, as mawquf upon Ka'b ibn Malik.
5. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and al-Hakim from the narration of al-Hajjaj ibn Artat from Abu Mudarr from Salim ibn 'Abd God from his father. Al-Tirmidhi said: gharib.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «خوفا وطمعا لا يصح أن يكون مفعولا لهما لأنهما ليسا بفعل
…. الخ» قال أحمد: أو مفعولا لهما، على أن المفعول له في مثل هذا الفعل فاعل في المعنى، لأنه إذا أراهم فقد رأوا، والأصل: وهو الذي يريكم البرق فترونه خوفاً وطمعاً، أى: ترقبونه وتتراءونه، تارة لأجل الخوف وتارة لأجل الطمع، والله أعلم.
2. . يقول: هو فتى شجاع جواد، يخشى شره، ويرجى خيره، فهو كالسحاب الأسود. والجون: الأسود: ويطلق على الأبيض. ورواه ابن جنى بالضم ليكون جمعا، أى السود المظلمات، لأن السحاب جمع في المعنى. يرتجى الحياء: أى المطر، منها. ونخشى صواعقها، وهي قطع النار التي تنزل منها.
3. . قوله «ومن له بيت يكف» وكف البيت يكف: قطر يقطر، كذا في الصحاح. (ع)
4. . أخرجه الطبري من رواية إسرائيل عن ليث عن رجل عن أبى هريرة رفعه «أنه كان إذا سمع الرعد قال سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده» ورواه البخاري في الأدب المفرد، موقوفا على كعب بن مالك.
5. . أخرجه الترمذي والنسائي وأحمد وأبو يعلى والحاكم من رواية الحجاج بن أرطاة عن أبى مضر عن سالم ابن عبد الله عن أبيه قال الترمذي: غريب.
Vol. 2, p. 519
1. (1) . His statement “ma'ahu makhariq min nar”: in al-Sihah: “al-mikhraq”: a handkerchief wound up to be struck with. (ʿ) [.....]
2. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ahmad from the narration of Bakr ibn Shihab from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: “The Jews approached the Prophet ﷺ and said: Tell us, O Abu al-Qasim, about the thunder. And he mentioned it — and added: They said: And what is this sound? He said: His rebuking of the cloud. They said: You have spoken truly.” And in al-Tabarani, in al-Awsat, from the narration of Abu 'Imran al-Kufi from Ibn Jurayj and from 'Ata' from Jabir, that Khuzayma ibn Thabit — and he is not the Ansari — “asked the Prophet ﷺ about thunder. He said: It is an angel in whose hand is a mikhraq; when he raises it, lightning flashes, and when he rebukes, it thunders, and when he strikes, it thunderbolts.”
3. His statement “bi-ghudda ka-ghuddat al-ba'ir”: in al-Sihah: “ghuddat al-ba'ir”: its plague. (ʿ)
4. Narrated by al-Tha'labi from the narration of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas. And al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from him from the narration of Zayd ibn Aslam from 'Ata' from him: “that Arbad ibn Qays and 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl came to Medina — and he mentioned the hadith at length.” And al-Nasa'i, al-Tabari, al-'Uqayli and Abu Ya'la narrated it from the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Sara from Thabit from Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God ﷺ sent a man to a man of the Khuza'a of the Arabs and said: Call him. He said: O Messenger of God, he is my brother in that [respect]. He said: Go and call him. So he came to him and said: The Messenger of God ﷺ is calling you. He said: And what is God? Is He of gold, or of silver, or of brass — the hadith. And in it: So God the Exalted revealed ‘and He sends thunderbolts’ … the verse.” Al-'Uqayli said: “Nothing prevents his hadith except from one lower than him.” And al-Bazzar and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated it from the narration of Daylam ibn Ghazwan from Thabit, similarly.
5. I say: What is in the hadith is “The Qur'an is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted, and a disputant who is believed” — narrated by Ibn Hibban from the narration of Abu Sufyan from Jabir, and by al-Hakim from the hadith of Ma'qil ibn Yasar, and by al-Tabarani from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, from Anas. Abu 'Ubayd narrated it in Fada'il al-Qur'an.
1. (1) . قوله «معه مخاريق من نار» في الصحاح المخراق: منديل يلف ليضرب به. (ع) [.....]
2. . أخرجه الترمذي والنسائي وأحمد من رواية بكر بن شهاب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال «أقبلت يهود إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: أخبرنا يا أبا القاسم عن الرعد. فذكره- وزاد: قالوا: فما هذا الصوت قال: زجره للسحاب قالوا: صدقت» وفي الطبراني والأوسط من رواية أبى عمران الكوفي عن ابن جريج وعن عطاء عن جابر أن خزيمة بن ثابت وليس بالأنصارى «سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الرعد. فقال: هو ملك بيده مخراق إذا رفع برق وإذا زجر رعدت وإذا ضرب صعقت،.
3. . قوله «بغدة كغدة البعير» في الصحاح: غدة البعير: طاعونه. (ع)
4. . أخرجه الثعلبي من رواية الكلبي عن أبى صالح عن ابن عباس. وأخرجه الطبراني وابن مردويه عنه من رواية زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء عنه «أن أريد بن قيس وعامر بن الطفيل قدما المدينة- فذكر الحديث مطولا» وأخرجه النسائي والطبري والعقيلي وأبو يعلى من رواية على بن أبى سارة عن ثابت عن أنس قال «بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا إلى رجل من خزاعة العرب فقال: ادعه قال: يا رسول الله هو أخى من ذلك. قال: اذهب فادعه. فأتاه. فقال: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعوك. قال: وما الله؟ أمن ذهب هو أو من فضة، أم من نحاس- الحديث. وفيه: فأنزل الله تعالى وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّواعِقَ
…. الآية قال العقيلي: لا مانع على حديثه إلا ممن هو دونه. وقد رواه البزار والبيهقي في الدلائل من رواية ديلم بن غزوان عن ثابت نحوه.
5. . قلت: الذي في الحديث «القرآن شافع مشفع وما حل مصدق» أخرجه ابن حبان من رواية أبى سفيان عن جابر والحاكم من حديث معقل بن يسار، والطبراني من حديث ابن مسعود عن أنس. أخرجه أبو عبيد في فضائل القرآن.
Vol. 2, p. 520
1. (1) . “Far'” of anything: its top. And “al-nab'”: a tree from which bows are made. And “al-hashsh” of anything: what has softness and suppleness. And “hashsha ilayhi” (of the type ta'iba and daraba): he laughed and beamed toward him; i.e. he is like the branch of the nab' in height and in hardness in wars. And he likened glory to a good tree by way of implicit metaphor (makniyya), so the annexation of the bough to it is an imaginative representation of that. It is possible that he likened his people to the boughs of the fruit-bearing tree by way of explicit metaphor (musarraha), and the annexation of them to glory is an indication of that. And in it is an indication that glory from them is like fruit from the boughs; “abundant of dew”: plentiful in giving; “severe in al-mihal,” i.e. al-mumahala and scheming; and it is like an explanation of the first likeness, and “abundant of dew” is like the explanation of the second; and it is among the marvels of speech.
2. His statement “wa-yajuzu an yakuna al-ma'na shadid al-fiqar”: in al-Sihah: “al-mahala” also: the vertebra, and in it “al-fiqara” is the singular of “fiqar” of the back. (ʿ)
3. Mahmud said: “There are two aspects: one, that the call be annexed to the truth … etc.” Ahmad said: He slipped under the interpretation of the first a morsel of Mu'tazilism in condensed form. So he confined what is wide of God's kindness and His answering the supplications of His servants, and made obligatory the observance of interests, and made the meaning of annexing the call to the truth its connection with interest; whereas the veil has been lifted and it has become clear that God the Exalted's acts are not given causes, and His answering does not depend on the stated condition. Our aim is to awaken the reader of these passages from a heedlessness by which one leans toward innovation and misguidance; and God is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . فرع كل شيء أعلاه. والنبع: شجر تتخذ منه القسي. والهش من كل شيء: ما فيه رخاوة وليونة. وهش إليه، من باب تعب وضرب: ضحك وانبسط إليه، أى هو كفرع النبع في العلو وللصلابة في الحروب. وشبه المجد بشجرة طيبة على طريق المكنية، فاضافة الغصن إليه تخييل لذلك. ويحتمل أنه شبه قومه بأغصان الشجرة المثمرة على طريق التصريحية، وإضافتها للمجد قرينة على ذلك. وفيها دلالة على أن المجد منهم كالثمر من الأغصان، غزير الندى كثير العطاء شديد المحال، أى المماحلة والمكايدة، وهو كالتفسير التشبيه الأول، وغزير الندى كالتفسير الثاني، وهو من بديع الكلام.
2. . قوله «ويجوز أن يكون المعنى شديد الفقار» في الصحاح: والمحالة أيضا: الفقارة، وفيه «الفقارة» واحدة فقار الظهر. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «فيه وجهان: أحدهما أن تضاف الدعوة إلى الحق
…. الخ» قال أحمد: دس تحت تأويل الأول نبذة من الاعتزال على وجه الاختزال. فحجر واسعاً من لطف الله واستجابته أدعية عباده، وحتم رعاية المصالح، وجعل معنى إضافة الدعوة إلى الحق التباسها بالمصلحة، وقد انكشف الغطاء وتبين أن الله تعالى لا تعلل أفعاله ولا تقف استجابته على الشرط المذكور، وغرضنا إيقاظ المطالع لهذه المواضع من غفلة يتحيز بها إلى بدعة وضلالة، والله الموفق.

Q 13:14 · Vol. 2, pp. 520–521

Verse 14

The verse as the commentary quotes it
To Him belongs the call of truth. And those whom they invoke besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except as one who stretches his hands toward water that it may reach his mouth, but it does not reach it. And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error (14)
لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الْحَقِّ وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ إِلاَّ كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى الْماءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فاهُ وَما هُوَ بِبالِغِهِ وَما دُعاءُ الْكافِرِينَ إِلاَّ فِي ضَلالٍ (14)
Vol. 2, p. 520
“da'wat al-haqq”: there are two aspects here. One, that the “da'wa” is annexed to “al-haqq” (3), which is the opposite of falsehood, as “word” is annexed to it in your saying “kalimat al-haqq,” to indicate that the call is bound up with truth and specific to it, and that it is far from falsehood. And the meaning is that God Glorified is invoked and answers the call, and gives the supplicant his request if it is of benefit to him, so it is a call connected with truth, since He is worthy that supplication be directed to Him, for the usefulness and benefit in calling Him, unlike one whose supplication is of no benefit or use. The second: that
دَعْوَةُ الْحَقِّ فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن تضاف الدعوة إلى الحق «3» الذي هو نقيض الباطل، كما تضاف الكلمة إليه في قولك: كلمة الحق، للدلالة على أن الدعوة ملابسة للحق مختصة به، وأنها بمعزل من الباطل. والمعنى أن الله سبحانه يدعى فيستجيب الدعوة، ويعطى الداعي سؤاله إن كان مصلحة له، فكانت دعوة ملابسة للحق، لكونه حقيقاً بأن يوجه إليه الدعاء، لما في دعوته من الجدوى والنفع، بخلاف ما لا ينفع ولا يجدى دعاؤه. والثاني: أن
Vol. 2, p. 521
is annexed to the Truth who is God, Mighty and Exalted, in the sense: the call of the One called upon, the Truth, who hears and answers. From al-Hasan: al-Haqq is God, and every supplication to Him is the call of truth. If you say: what is the connection of these two descriptions with what precedes (1)? I say: As for the story of Arbad, it is clear, because his being struck by the thunderbolt was a stratagem from God and a plot against him from where he did not perceive. And the Messenger of God ﷺ had supplicated against him and against his companion with his words: “O God, sink them both by whatever You will,” so it was answered regarding them (2), and so the call was a call of truth. And as for the first [aspect], it is a threat to the disbelievers, for their disputing with the Messenger of God, by the descent of His stratagems upon them, and by the answering of the supplication of the Messenger of God ﷺ when he supplicated against them. “and those who call” — the gods whom the disbelievers call “besides God” — “do not respond to them with anything” of their requests “except as one who stretches out his hands” — except [with] a response like the response of water to one who stretches out his hands to it, asking it to reach his mouth; and water is inanimate and is not aware of his stretching out his hands, nor of his thirst and his need for it, and it is not able to answer his call and reach his mouth; and likewise what they invoke is inanimate, which does not sense their supplication and cannot answer them and is unable to benefit them. And it is said: they were likened, in the paltry usefulness of their supplication to their gods, to one who wants to scoop water with his hands to drink it, so he stretched them out, spreading his fingers, and his palms did not catch any of it and he did not reach his aim of drinking it. It is read: “tad'un,” with ta'. “ka-basiti kaffayhi,” with tanwin. “except in error”: except in loss in which there is no benefit, because if they call upon God He does not answer them, and if they call upon the gods they cannot answer them.
تضاف إلى الحق الذي هو الله عز وعلا، على معنى: دعوة المدعوّ الحق الذي يسمع فيجيب. وعن الحسن: الحق هو الله، وكلّ دعاء إليه دعوة الحق. فإن قلت: ما وجه اتصال هذين الوصفين بما قبله «1» ؟ قلت. أما على قصة أربد فظاهر، لأن إصابته بالصاعقة محال من الله ومكر به من حيث لم يشعر. وقد دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليه وعلى صاحبه بقوله: اللهمّ اخسفهما بما شئت، فأجيب فيهما «2» ، فكانت الدعوة دعوة حق. وأما على الأوّل فوعيد للكفرة على مجادلتهم رسول الله بحلول محاله بهم، وإجابة دعوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن دعا عليهم فيهم وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ والآلهة الذين يدعوهم الكفار مِنْ دون الله لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ من طلباتهم إِلَّا كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إلا استجابة كاستجابة باسط كفيه، أى كاستجابة الماء من بسط كفيه إليه يطلب منه أن يبلغ فاه، والماء جماد لا يشعر ببسط كفيه ولا بعطشه وحاجته إليه، ولا يقدر أن يجيب دعاءه ويبلغ فاه، وكذلك ما يدعونه جماد لا يحس بدعائهم ولا يستطيع إجابتهم ولا يقدر على نفعهم. وقيل: شبهوا في قلة جدوى دعائهم لآلهتهم بمن أراد أن يغرف الماء بيديه ليشربه، فبسطهما ناشراً أصابعه، فلم تلق كفاه منه شيئاً ولم يبلغ طلبته من شربه. وقرئ: تدعون، بالتاء. كباسط كفيه، بالتنوين إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ إلا في ضياع لا منفعة فيه، لأنهم إن دعوا الله لم يجبهم، وإن دعوا الآلهة لم تستطع إجابتهم.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 520
1. (1) . “Far'” of anything: its top. And “al-nab'”: a tree from which bows are made. And “al-hashsh” of anything: what has softness and suppleness. And “hashsha ilayhi” (of the type ta'iba and daraba): he laughed and beamed toward him; i.e. he is like the branch of the nab' in height and in hardness in wars. And he likened glory to a good tree by way of implicit metaphor (makniyya), so the annexation of the bough to it is an imaginative representation of that. It is possible that he likened his people to the boughs of the fruit-bearing tree by way of explicit metaphor (musarraha), and the annexation of them to glory is an indication of that. And in it is an indication that glory from them is like fruit from the boughs; “abundant of dew”: plentiful in giving; “severe in al-mihal,” i.e. al-mumahala and scheming; and it is like an explanation of the first likeness, and “abundant of dew” is like the explanation of the second; and it is among the marvels of speech.
2. His statement “wa-yajuzu an yakuna al-ma'na shadid al-fiqar”: in al-Sihah: “al-mahala” also: the vertebra, and in it “al-fiqara” is the singular of “fiqar” of the back. (ʿ)
3. Mahmud said: “There are two aspects: one, that the call be annexed to the truth … etc.” Ahmad said: He slipped under the interpretation of the first a morsel of Mu'tazilism in condensed form. So he confined what is wide of God's kindness and His answering the supplications of His servants, and made obligatory the observance of interests, and made the meaning of annexing the call to the truth its connection with interest; whereas the veil has been lifted and it has become clear that God the Exalted's acts are not given causes, and His answering does not depend on the stated condition. Our aim is to awaken the reader of these passages from a heedlessness by which one leans toward innovation and misguidance; and God is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . فرع كل شيء أعلاه. والنبع: شجر تتخذ منه القسي. والهش من كل شيء: ما فيه رخاوة وليونة. وهش إليه، من باب تعب وضرب: ضحك وانبسط إليه، أى هو كفرع النبع في العلو وللصلابة في الحروب. وشبه المجد بشجرة طيبة على طريق المكنية، فاضافة الغصن إليه تخييل لذلك. ويحتمل أنه شبه قومه بأغصان الشجرة المثمرة على طريق التصريحية، وإضافتها للمجد قرينة على ذلك. وفيها دلالة على أن المجد منهم كالثمر من الأغصان، غزير الندى كثير العطاء شديد المحال، أى المماحلة والمكايدة، وهو كالتفسير التشبيه الأول، وغزير الندى كالتفسير الثاني، وهو من بديع الكلام.
2. . قوله «ويجوز أن يكون المعنى شديد الفقار» في الصحاح: والمحالة أيضا: الفقارة، وفيه «الفقارة» واحدة فقار الظهر. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «فيه وجهان: أحدهما أن تضاف الدعوة إلى الحق
…. الخ» قال أحمد: دس تحت تأويل الأول نبذة من الاعتزال على وجه الاختزال. فحجر واسعاً من لطف الله واستجابته أدعية عباده، وحتم رعاية المصالح، وجعل معنى إضافة الدعوة إلى الحق التباسها بالمصلحة، وقد انكشف الغطاء وتبين أن الله تعالى لا تعلل أفعاله ولا تقف استجابته على الشرط المذكور، وغرضنا إيقاظ المطالع لهذه المواضع من غفلة يتحيز بها إلى بدعة وضلالة، والله الموفق.
Vol. 2, p. 521
1. (1) . His statement “the connection of these two descriptions with what precedes”: the wording of al-Nasafi is: “and the connection of ‘severe in al-mihal’ and ‘to Him belongs the call of truth’ with what precedes it.” (ʿ)
2. Al-Wahidi mentioned it in al-Asbab from Ibn 'Abbas in the aforementioned story. But I did not see it in it in the two previous routes, from the narration of al-Kalbi and others.

Q 13:15 · Vol. 2, p. 521

Verse 15

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings (15)
وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً وَظِلالُهُمْ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصالِ (15)
Vol. 2, p. 521
“And to God prostrates”: i.e. they submit to the bringing about in them of what He intends of His acts, whether they will or not. They cannot refuse Him; and their shadows also submit to Him, as they move according to His will in extension and contraction, in shade and disappearance. It is read: “bi-l-ghuduwwi wa-l-i'sal,” from “asalu” when they enter the late afternoon.
وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ أى ينقادون لإحداث ما أراده فيهم من أفعاله، شاءوا أو أبوا. لا يقدرون أن يمتنعوا عليه، وتنقاد له ظِلالُهُمْ أيضاً، حيث تتصرف على مشيئته في الامتداد والتقلص، والفيء والزوال. وقرئ: بالغدوّ والإيصال، من آصلوا: إذا دخلوا في الأصيل.

Q 13:16 · Vol. 2, pp. 521–522

Verse 16

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: God. Say: Then have you taken besides Him protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm? Say: Is the blind equal to the seeing? Or is darkness equal to light? Or have they made for God partners who created like His creation, so that the creation seemed alike to them? Say: God is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer (16)
قُلْ مَنْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ لا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ نَفْعاً وَلا ضَرًّا قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُماتُ وَالنُّورُ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ قُلِ اللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْواحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ (16)
Vol. 2, p. 522
“Say: God” is a narration of their admission and a confirmation against them, because if He says to them “Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth,” they have no choice but to say God, as in His saying “Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne? They will say: To God.” And this is like a debater saying to his opponent: Is this your statement? And when he says: This is my statement, he says: This is your statement — narrating his admission by way of confirming it against him and securing it from him; then he says to him: So there follows from this statement of yours such and such. It is also possible that it is a prompting, i.e.: if they hold back from the answer (1), then prompt them, for they will accept the prompt and be unable to deny it. “Then have you taken besides Him protectors”: after you have known Him as Lord of the heavens and the earth, have you taken besides Him protectors? — so you made what ought to have been the cause of monotheism, from your knowledge and your admission, the cause of polytheism! “who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm”: they are unable to benefit themselves or to avert harm from themselves, so how can they do it for others, when you have preferred them over the Creator, Provider, Rewarder, Punisher? How manifest is your misguidance! “Or have they made”: rather, make [it so]. And the meaning of the hamza is denial (2); and “they created” is a description of “partners,” meaning that they did not take for God partners who are creators and who created like God's creation, so that “the creation seemed alike to them” — God's creation and their creation — so that they would say: These are able to create as God is able, so they deserved worship, so we take them as partners with Him and worship them as He is worshipped, since there is no difference between creator and creator; but rather they took for Him partners who are powerless, unable to do what creatures are able to do, let alone to do what the Creator is able to do. “Say: God is the Creator of all things”: there is no creator other than God, and it is not sound that He have a partner in creation, so He has no partner in worship. “and He is the One”: unique in lordship; “the Subduer”: not overcome; and everything other than Him is ruled and subdued.
قُلِ اللَّهُ حكاية لاعترافهم وتأكيد لم عليهم، لأنه إذا قال لهم: من رب السموات والأرض، لم يكن لهم بدّ من أن يقولوا الله. كقوله قُلْ مَنْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ السَّبْعِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ وهذا كما يقول المناظر لصاحبه: أهذا قولك، فإذا قال: هذا قولي قال: هذا قولك، فيحكى إقراره تقريراً له عليه واستيثاقا منه، ثم يقول له: فيلزمك على هذا القول كيت وكيت. ويجوز أن يكون تلقيناً، أى: إن كعوا عن الجواب «1» فلقنهم، فإنهم يتلقنونه ولا يقدرون أن ينكروه أَفَاتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ أبعد أن علمتموه رب السموات والأرض اتخذتم من دونه أولياء، فجعلتم ما كان يجب أن يكون سبب التوحيد من علمكم وإقراركم سبب الإشراك لا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ نَفْعاً وَلا ضَرًّا لا يستطيعون لأنفسهم أن ينفعوها أو يدفعوا عنها ضررا، فكيف يستطيعونه لغيرهم وقد آثرتموهم على الخالق الرازق المثيب المعاقب، فما أبين ضلالتكم! أَمْ جَعَلُوا بل اجعلوا. ومعنى الهمزة الإنكار «2» وخَلَقُوا صفة لشركاء، يعنى أنهم لم يتخذوا لله شركاء خالقين قد خلقوا مثل خلق الله فَتَشابَهَ عليهم خلق الله وخلقهم، حتى يقولوا: قدر هؤلاء على الخلق كما قدر الله عليه، فاستحقوا العبادة، فنتخذهم له شركاء ونعبدهم كما يعبد، إذ لا فرق بين خالق وخالق، ولكنهم اتخذوا له شركاء عاجزين لا يقدرون على ما يقدر عليه الخلق، فضلا أن يقدروا على ما يقدر عليه الخالق قُلِ اللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لا خالق غير الله، ولا يستقيم أن يكون له شريك في الخلق، فلا يكون له شريك في العبادة وَهُوَ الْواحِدُ المتوحد بالربوبية الْقَهَّارُ لا يغالب، وما عداه مربوب ومقهور.
