1. (1) . His statement “ay in ka'u 'an al-jawab”: i.e. they refrained out of cowardice or were held back. So al-Sihah states. (ʿ)
2. Mahmud said: “‘Am’ is estimated as ‘bal’ and the hamza, and its meaning here is denial … etc.” Ahmad said: And in His saying “created like His creation,” in the context of denial, there is mockery of them, because other than God does not create any creation at all — neither by way of resemblance and equality to God, Glory be to Him above likeness, nor by way of inferiority and shortfall; so it would have sufficed in rebuking them that the partners they took do not create at all, but there came in His saying “like His creation” a mockery that increases the denial in emphasis. And al-Zamakhshari cannot bear to point out this subtlety, though he is too perceptive for it to be hidden from him, because his belief is that other than God creates, namely the servants create their acts, in his claim, but they do not create like God's creation, because God the Exalted creates substances and accidents, whereas the servants create nothing but their acts and nothing else. And in the saying of the One glorified in speech “God is the Creator of all things” is a muzzling of the mouths of the first polytheists, then of the mouths of those who follow them in this misguidance, like the Qadariyya; for God the Exalted decided this decisively: that everything of which it is truly said that it is created, whether a substance or an accident, an act of His servants or other than it, God is its Creator, so no remainder is left in which association could be allowed, except in the view of every sinful liar who hears the verses of God recited to him and then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard them, as if in his ears were deafness — so give him tidings of a painful punishment. So for some reason al-Zamakhshari's tongue fell short at this verse and he kept his bluster in check; and God is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . قوله «أى إن كعوا عن الجواب» أى امتنعوا جبناً أو احتبسوا. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «أم مقدرة ببل والهمزة ومعناها هاهنا الإنكار
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وفي قوله تعالى خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ في سياق الإنكار تهكم بهم، لأن غير الله لا يخلق خلقا البتة، لا بطريق المشابهة والمساواة لله- تقدس عن التشبيه- ولا بطريق الانحطاط والقصور، فقد كان يكفى في الإنكار عليهم أن الشركاء التي اتخذوها لا تخلق مطلقا، ولكن جاء في قوله تعالى كَخَلْقِهِ تهكم يزيد الإنكار تأكيداً. والزمخشري لا يطيق التنبيه على هذه النكتة مع كونه أفطن من أن تستتر عنه، لأن معتقده أن غير الله يخلق وهم العبيد يخلقون أفعالهم على زعمه، ولكن لا يخلقون كخلق الله، لأن الله تعالى يخلق الجواهر والأعراض، والعبيد لا يخلقون سوى أفعالهم لا غير. وفي قوله عز من قائل اللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ إلقام لأفواه المشركين الأولين، ثم لأفواه التابعة لهم في هذه الضلالة كالقدرية، فان الله تعالى بت هذه البتة أن كل شيء يصدق عليه أنه مخلوق جوهراً كان أو عرضا، فعلا لعبيده أو غيره، فالله خالقه، فلا يبقى بقية يحتمل معها الاشتراك إلا عند كل أثيم أفاك، يسمع آيات الله تتلى عليه ثم يصر مستكبراً كأن لم يسمعها، كأن في أذنيه وقرا فبشره بعذاب أليم، فلأمر ما تقاصر لسان الزمخشري عند هذه الآية وقرن شقاشقه، والله الموفق.
14
Q 13:17 · Vol. 2, pp. 522–524

Verse 17

The verse as the commentary quotes it
He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam; and from that which they heat in the fire, seeking ornaments or utensils, is a foam like it. Thus does God present the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes as dross; and as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus does God present parables (17)
أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَسالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِها فَاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَداً رابِياً وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتاعٍ زَبَدٌ مِثْلُهُ كَذلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ وَالْباطِلَ فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفاءً وَأَمَّا ما يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ كَذلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثالَ (17)
Vol. 2, p. 523
This is a parable that God struck for the truth and its people and for falsehood and its party, as He struck the blind and the seeing and the darknesses and the light as a parable for them. So He likened the truth and its people to the water which He sends down from the sky, so that people's valleys flow with it and they live by it and various kinds of benefits accrue to them, and to the smelted metal from which they benefit (1) in casting ornaments from it and making vessels and various tools — and if there were nothing but iron, in which is mighty power, it would suffice; and that this remains on the earth, lasting in manifest permanence: the water stays fixed in its benefits, and its traces remain in springs, wells and tanks, and the fruits that grow by it, of what is stored and hoarded; and likewise the substances remain for long ages. And He likened falsehood, in the speed of its dissipation, the nearness of its vanishing and its stripping off from benefit, to the foam of the torrent that is cast off, and to the foam of the metal that floats above it when it is melted.
هذا مثل ضربه الله للحق وأهله والباطل وحزبه، كما ضرب الأعمى والبصير والظلمات والنور مثلا لهما، فمثل الحق وأهله بالماء الذي ينزله من السماء فتسيل به أودية الناس فيحيون به وينفعهم أنواع المنافع، وبالفلز الذي ينتفعون به «1» في صوغ الحلىّ منه واتخاذ الأوانى والآلات المختلفة، ولو لم يكن إلا الحديد الذي فيه البأس الشديد لكفى به، وأن ذلك ماكث في الأرض باق بقاء ظاهراً، يثبت الماء في منافعه. وتبقى آثاره في العيون والبئار والجبوب، والثمار التي تنبت به مما يدّخر ويكنز، وكذلك الجواهر تبقى أزمنة متطاولة. وشبه الباطل في سرعة اضمحلاله ووشك زواله وانسلاخه عن المنفعة، بزيد السيل الذي يرمى به، وبزبد الفلز الذي يطفو فوقه إذا أذيب.
Question
If you say: why were the valleys indefinite?
فإن قلت: لم نكرت الأودية؟
Answer
I say: because rain comes only by way of rotation among the lands, so some valleys of the earth flow and not others.
قلت: لأن المطر لا يأتى إلا على طريق المناوبة بين البقاع، فيسيل بعض أودية الأرض دون بعض.
Question
If you say: what is the meaning of His saying “bi-qadariha”?
فإن قلت: فما معنى قوله بِقَدَرِها؟
Answer
I say: by their measure which God knew to be beneficial to those rained upon and not harmful. Do you not see His saying “and as for that which benefits the people,” because He struck rain as a parable for truth, so it had to be rain purely beneficial, free of harm, not like some rains and sweeping torrents (2).
قلت: بمقدارها الذي عرف الله أنه نافع للممطور عليهم غير ضارّ. ألا ترى إلى قوله وَأَمَّا ما يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ لأنه ضرب المطر مثلا للحق، فوجب أن يكون مطراً خالصاً للنفع خالياً من المضرة، ولا يكون كبعض الأمطار والسيول الجواحف «2» .
Question
If you say: what is the benefit of His saying “seeking ornaments or utensils”?
فإن قلت: فما فائدة قوله ابْتِغاءَ حلية أو متاع؟
Answer
I say: the benefit in it is like the benefit in “bi-qadariha,” because He combined water and metal in benefit in His saying “and as for that which benefits the people,” since the meaning is: and as for what benefits them of water and metal, so He mentioned the aspect of benefit from what is heated and melted of it, which is ornaments and utensils. And His saying “and from that which they heat in the fire, seeking ornaments or utensils” is a comprehensive expression for the kinds of metal, while showing grandeur in mentioning it with a tone of disdain for it, as is the habit of kings, like what came in the mention of baked brick: “So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay.” And “min” is for the beginning of the range, i.e. from it arises a foam like the foam of water; or it is partitive, in the sense of: and some of it is a swelling foam, puffed up, rising on the surface of the torrent, i.e. cast off. And “jafa'tu al-qidr bi-zabadiha” [I skimmed the pot of its foam], and “ajfa'a al-sayl” and “ajfala.” And in the reading of Ru'ba ibn al-'Ajjaj: “jufalan.” And from Abu Hatim: one does not read with the reading of Ru'ba, because he used to eat mice. It is also read: “yuqidun,” with ya': i.e. people heat.
قلت: الفائدة فيه كالفائدة في قوله بِقَدَرِها لأنه جمع الماء والفلز في النفع في قوله وَأَمَّا ما يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ لأنّ المعنى: وأما ما ينفعهم من الماء والفلز فذكر وجه الانتفاع مما يوقد عليه منه ويذاب، وهو الحلية والمتاع. وقوله وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتاعٍ عبارة جامعة لأنواع الفلز، مع إظهار الكبرياء في ذكره على وجه التهاون به كما هو هجيرى الملوك، نحو ما جاء في ذكر الآجر فَأَوْقِدْ لِي يا هامانُ عَلَى الطِّينِ و «من» لابتداء الغاية. أى: ومنه ينشأ زبد مثل زبد الماء. أو للتبعيض بمعنى وبعضه زبداً رابياً منفخاً مرتفعاً على وجه السيل، أى يرمى به. وجفأت القدر بزبدها، وأجفأ السيل وأجفل. وفي قراءة رؤبة ابن العجاج: جفالا. وعن أبى حاتم: لا يقرأ بقراءة رؤبة، لأنه كان يأكل الفأر. وقرئ: يوقدون، بالياء: أى يوقد الناس.
Vol. 2, p. 524
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 522
1. (1) . His statement “ay in ka'u 'an al-jawab”: i.e. they refrained out of cowardice or were held back. So al-Sihah states. (ʿ)
2. Mahmud said: “‘Am’ is estimated as ‘bal’ and the hamza, and its meaning here is denial … etc.” Ahmad said: And in His saying “created like His creation,” in the context of denial, there is mockery of them, because other than God does not create any creation at all — neither by way of resemblance and equality to God, Glory be to Him above likeness, nor by way of inferiority and shortfall; so it would have sufficed in rebuking them that the partners they took do not create at all, but there came in His saying “like His creation” a mockery that increases the denial in emphasis. And al-Zamakhshari cannot bear to point out this subtlety, though he is too perceptive for it to be hidden from him, because his belief is that other than God creates, namely the servants create their acts, in his claim, but they do not create like God's creation, because God the Exalted creates substances and accidents, whereas the servants create nothing but their acts and nothing else. And in the saying of the One glorified in speech “God is the Creator of all things” is a muzzling of the mouths of the first polytheists, then of the mouths of those who follow them in this misguidance, like the Qadariyya; for God the Exalted decided this decisively: that everything of which it is truly said that it is created, whether a substance or an accident, an act of His servants or other than it, God is its Creator, so no remainder is left in which association could be allowed, except in the view of every sinful liar who hears the verses of God recited to him and then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard them, as if in his ears were deafness — so give him tidings of a painful punishment. So for some reason al-Zamakhshari's tongue fell short at this verse and he kept his bluster in check; and God is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . قوله «أى إن كعوا عن الجواب» أى امتنعوا جبناً أو احتبسوا. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)

1. (1) . His statement “wa-bi-l-falaz alladhi yantafi'una bihi”: in al-Sihah: “al-falaz” (with kasra and shaddah on the za'): what the bellows expels of what is melted of the substances of the earth; end. Let it be corrected, and perhaps it is “what the bellows leaves” … etc. (ʿ)
2. His statement “al-suyul al-jawahif”: in al-Sihah: “sayl juhaf” (with damma): when it sweeps away everything and carries it off. (ʿ)

…. الخ. (ع)

Q 13:18 · Vol. 2, p. 524

Verse 18

The verse as the commentary quotes it
For those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]. And those who did not respond to Him — if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom. Those will have an evil reckoning, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place (18)
لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنى وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُ لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لافْتَدَوْا بِهِ أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْحِسابِ وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ (18)
Vol. 2, p. 524
“For those who responded”: the lam is connected to “yadribu”: i.e. thus does God present parables for the believers who responded and for the disbelievers who did not respond, i.e. the two are the parables of the two groups. And “al-husna” is a description of a verbal noun for “istajabu”: i.e. they responded the best response. And His saying “if they had” is a new sentence in mention of what is prepared for those who do not respond. And it is said: the speech was complete at His saying “thus does God present parables,” and what follows is a new sentence. And “al-husna” is a subject, whose predicate is “for those who responded”; and the meaning: for them is the best reward, which is Paradise. “And those who did not respond” is a subject, whose predicate is “lau” with what is in its scope. And “su' al-hisab”: strictness in it. And from al-Nakha'i: that a man be reckoned for all his sins, none of it being forgiven.
لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا اللام متعلقة بيضرب، أى كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال للمؤمنين الذين استجابوا، وللكافرين الذين لم يستجيبوا، أى: هما مثلا الفريقين. والْحُسْنى صفة لمصدر استجابوا، أى: استجابوا الاستجابة الحسنى. وقوله لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ كلام مبتدأ في ذكر ما أعدّ لغير المستجيبين. وقيل: قد تم الكلام عند قوله كَذلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثالَ وما بعده كلام مستأنف. والحسنى: مبتدأ، خبره لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا والمعنى: لهم المثوبة الحسنى، وهي الجنة وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا مبتدأ خبره. «لو» مع ما في حيزه وسُوءُ الْحِسابِ المناقشة فيه. وعن النخعي: أن يحاسب الرجل بذنبه كله لا يغفر منه شيء
16
Q 13:19 · Vol. 2, p. 524

Verse 19

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Then is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those of understanding remember (19)
أَفَمَنْ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ كَمَنْ هُوَ أَعْمى إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ (19)
Vol. 2, p. 524
The hamza of denial entered upon the fa' in “a-fa-man ya'lam,” to deny that doubt should occur after the parable struck, that the state of one who knew that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth and responded is far removed from the state of the ignorant one who did not gain insight and so respond: like the distance between foam and water, and dross and pure gold. “Only those of understanding remember”: i.e. those who acted by the dictates of their intellects, so looked and gained insight.
دخلت همزة الإنكار على الفاء في قوله أَفَمَنْ يَعْلَمُ لإنكار أن تقع شبهة بعد ما ضرب من المثل في أنّ حال من علم أَنَّما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ فاستجاب، بمعزل من حال الجاهل الذي لم يستبصر فيستجيب: كبعد ما بين الزبد والماء والخبث والإبريز إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ أى الذين عملوا على قضيات عقولهم، فنظروا واستبصروا.
17
Q 13:20–24 · Vol. 2, pp. 524–527

Verses 20 to 24

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the pledge (20) And those who join that which God has ordered to be joined, and fear their Lord, and are afraid of the evil reckoning (21) And those who are patient, seeking the face of their Lord, and establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good — those will have the best end of the abode (22) Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants; and the angels will enter upon them from every gate (23) Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; and excellent is the final abode (24)
الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَلا يَنْقُضُونَ الْمِيثاقَ (20) وَالَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ وَيَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ وَيَخافُونَ سُوءَ الْحِسابِ (21) وَالَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ (22) جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبائِهِمْ وَأَزْواجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ بابٍ (23) سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِما صَبَرْتُمْ فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ (24)
Vol. 2, p. 525
“Those who fulfill the covenant of God” is a subject; and “those will have the best end of the abode” is its predicate, like His saying: “and those who break the covenant of God — those will have the curse.” It is also possible that it is a description of “those of understanding,” but the first is the stronger aspect. And “the covenant of God”: what they bound upon themselves of the testimony to His lordship — “and He made them bear witness over themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes.” “And do not break the pledge”: and they do not break anything they bound upon themselves and accepted: of faith in God and other pledges between them and God and between them and the servants — a generalization after a specification. “that which God has ordered to be joined”: of the wombs and kinships, and it includes joining the kinship of the Messenger of God and the kinship of the believers established by faith — “The believers are but brothers” — by doing good to them according to ability, and helping them, and defending them, and compassion for them, and sincere counsel to them, and casting away division between themselves and them, and spreading the greeting of peace upon them, and visiting their sick, and attending their funerals. And from it is observing the rights of companions, servants, neighbors and fellow-travelers, and everything connected with them by any tie, even the cat and the hen. From al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad: that a group entered upon him in Mecca and he said: From where are you? They said: From the people of Khurasan. He said: Fear God and be wherever you wish, and know that a servant, if he did all the good, and he had a hen and mistreated it, would not be among the doers of good. “and fear their Lord”: i.e. they fear all of His threat; “and they are afraid” especially “of the evil reckoning,” so they reckon themselves before they are reckoned. “They were patient” is unrestricted, in what is endured of afflictions to selves and wealth and the hardships of obligation, “seeking the face of God,” not so that it be said: how patient he is and how enduring of calamities, and how dignified in earthquakes; nor so as not to be faulted for impatience nor that enemies rejoice at his misfortune, like the saying: “and my fortitude before the gloaters I show them” (1); nor because there is no gain in anguish and no turning back of what is lost in it, like the saying: “I was not impatient nor did I wail … nor does my weeping bring back Zand” (2)
الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ مبتدأ. وأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ خبره كقوله: والذين ينقضون عهد الله أولئك لهم اللعنة. ويجوز أن يكون صفة لأولى الألباب، والأوّل أوجه. وعهد الله: ما عقدوه على أنفسهم من الشهادة بربوبيته وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قالُوا بَلى. وَلا يَنْقُضُونَ الْمِيثاقَ ولا ينقضون كل ما وثقوه على أنفسهم وقبلوه: من الإيمان بالله وغيره من المواثيق بينهم وبين الله وبين العباد، تعميم بعد تخصيص ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ من الأرحام والقرابات، ويدخل فيه وصل قرابة رسول الله وقرابة المؤمنين الثابتة بسبب الإيمان إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ بالإحسان إليهم على حسب الطاقة، ونصرتهم، والذب عنهم، والشفقة عليهم، والنصيحة لهم، وطرح التفرقة بين أنفسهم وبينهم، وإفشاء السلام عليهم، وعيادة مرضاهم، وشهود جنائزهم. ومنه مراعاة حق الأصحاب والخدم والجيران والرفقاء في السفر، وكل ما تعلق منهم بسبب، حتى الهرة والدجاجة. وعن الفضيل بن عياض أنّ جماعة دخلوا عليه بمكة فقال: من أين أنتم؟ قالوا: من أهل خراسان. قال: اتقوا الله وكونوا من حيث شئتم، واعلموا أنّ العبد لو أحسن الإحسان كله وكانت له دجاجة فأساء إليها لم يكن من المحسنين وَيَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ أى يخشون وعيده كله وَيَخافُونَ خصوصاً سُوءَ الْحِسابِ فيحاسبون أنفسهم قبل أن يحاسبوا صَبَرُوا مطلق فيما يصبر عليه من المصائب في النفوس والأموال ومشاق التكليف ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ الله، لا ليقال: ما أصبره وأحمله للنوازل، وأوقره عند الزلازل، ولا لئلا يعاب بالجزع ولئلا يشمت به الأعداء كقوله: وَتَجَلُّدِى لِلشّامِتِينَ أُرِيهِمُ «1» ولا لأنه لا طائل تحت الهلع ولا مردّ فيه للفائت، كقوله: مَا إنْ جَزِعْتُ وَلَا هَلَعْ … تُ وَلَا يَرُدُّ بُكَاىَ زَنْدَا «2»
Vol. 2, p. 526
Every deed has aspects upon which it is done, so the believer must intend of them that by which it is good with God; otherwise he does not deserve reward by it, and it is as though he did not do it. “Of what We have provided them” — of the lawful, because the unlawful is not provision (1) and is not attributed to God (2). “Secretly and publicly” includes supererogatory acts, since they are better in secret, and obligatory acts, for the necessity of making them public to avert suspicion. “And repel evil with good” — and ward it off. From Ibn Abbas: they repel with good speech the evil that comes to them from others. From al-Hasan: when they are denied, they give; when wronged, they pardon; when cut off, they connect. From Ibn Kaysan: when they sin, they repent. It is also said: when they see something objectionable they command its change. “The best end of the abode” — the outcome of this world, which is Paradise, because it is what God intended to be the outcome of this world and the destination of its people (3). And “gardens of Eden” is a substitute for “the end of the abode.” It was read: fa-ni'ma with fatha on the nun.
وكل عمل له وجوه يعمل عليها، فعلى المؤمن أن ينوى منها ما به كان حسناً عند الله، وإلا لم يستحق به ثواباً، وكان فعل كلا فعل مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ من الحلال، لأنّ الحرام لا يكون رزقا «1» ولا يسند إلى الله «2» سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً يتناول النوافل، لأنها في السر أفضل- والفرائض، لوجوب المجاهرة بها نفياً للتهمة وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ ويدفعونها. عن ابن عباس: يدفعون بالحسن من الكلام ما يرد عليهم من سيئ غيرهم. وعن الحسن: إذا حرموا أعطوا، وإذا ظلموا عفوا، وإذا قطعوا وصلوا. وعن ابن كيسان: إذا أذنبوا تابوا. وقيل: إذا رأوا منكراً أمروا بتغييره عُقْبَى الدَّارِ عاقبة الدنيا وهي الجنة، لأنها التي أراد الله أن تكون عاقبة الدنيا ومرجع أهلها «3» . وجَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ بدل من عقبى الدار. وقرئ: فنعم، بفتح النون.
Vol. 2, p. 527
and the original is ni'ma. So whoever put kasra on the nun transferred the kasra of the 'ayn to it; and whoever put fatha made the 'ayn sakin and did not transfer. It was read: yudkhalunaha in the passive. Ibn Abi 'Abla read salaha with damma on the lam; the fatha is more eloquent. Know that lineages do not benefit when stripped of righteous deeds. “Their fathers” is the plural of the two parents of each of them, as if it were said: of their fathers and mothers. “Peace be upon you” is in the position of a circumstantial clause, because the meaning is: saying “peace be upon you,” or greeting.
والأصل: نعم. فمن كسر النون فلنقل كسرة العين إليها، ومن فتح فقد سكن العين ولم ينقل وقرى: يَدْخُلُونَها على البناء للمفعول. وقرأ ابن أبى عبلة صَلَحَ بضم اللام، والفتح أفصح، أعلم أنّ الأنساب لا تنفع إذا تجردت من الأعمال الصالحة. وآباؤهم جمع أبوى كل واحد منهم، فكأنه قيل من آبائهم وأمهاتهم سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ في موضع الحال، لأنّ المعنى: قائلين سلام عليكم، أو مسلمين.
Question
If you ask: to what is “for what you patiently endured” connected?
فإن قلت: بم تعلق قوله بِما صَبَرْتُمْ؟
Answer
I say: to an omitted element, estimated: this is for what you endured, meaning this reward is because of your patience, or in return for the hardships and toils of patience that you bore, these pleasures and blessings. The meaning: if you toiled in the world, you have rested this very hour, as in the line: “for what I see in it, plump maidens” (1). From the Prophet ﷺ that he used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the turn of each year and say: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final abode” (2). It is also possible that it is connected with “peace,” i.e. we greet you and honor you for your patience.
قلت: بمحذوف تقديره: هذا بما صبرتم، يعنون هذا الثواب بسبب صبركم، أو بدل ما احتملتم من مشاق الصبر ومتاعبه هذه الملاذ والنعم. والمعنى: لئن تعبتم في الدنيا لقد استرحتم الساعة، كقوله: بِمَا قَدْ أرَى فِيهَا أوَانِسَ بُدَّنَا «1» وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأتى قبور الشهداء على رأس كل حول فيقول «السلام عليكم بما صبرتم فنعم عقبى الدار» «2» ويجوز أن يتعلق بسلام، أى نسلم عليكم ونكرمكم بصبركم.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 2, p. 525
1. (1) . “And when death has sunk its claws … you find every amulet useless. And my fortitude before the gloaters I show them … that I do not cringe before the vicissitudes of time.” By Abu Dhu'ayb Khuwaylid ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi [sic; the poet is generally known as al-Hudhali], mourning his sons. It is narrated that Mu'awiya fell ill, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ؓ both, visited him, and he said: Apply kohl to me and put on my turban for me, and he showed strength, and recited to him the second line, so al-Hasan answered him suddenly with the first. He likened death to a predator by way of implicit metaphor (makniyya), and the sinking of the claws is an imaginative representation of it. “Muniya lahu”: it was decreed for him. “Al-maniyya”: death, because it is decreed. “Al-inshab”: plunging and hanging. “Alfayta”: i.e. “you found every amulet useless” — and it is what is hung upon children for fear of the jinn and envy. And “tajalludi”: i.e. my patience and my hardening, a subject; and “uriyahum” is its predicate, i.e. I show them by it that I do not cringe and humble myself and weaken because of the vicissitudes of time, i.e. its occurrences that come from where I do not perceive. [.....]
2. “Beauty is not in a waist-wrapper … so know, even if you are clad in a burd, that beauty is mines [of worth] … and virtues that bequeath glory. I prepared for the vicissitudes an ample coat of mail … and a fast-running mare, a tough, massive, swift one, and one with sword-streaks that cuts … helmets and body-armors through. How many a righteous brother of mine … I lodged with my own hands in a grave. I did not wail, nor did I grieve … nor does my weeping bring back Zand.” By 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib. He says: beauty is not in splendid garments. And “fa'lam” is parenthetical. The address is to no one in particular, i.e. it is not so even if you clothe it. “Al-burd”: an ample garment that one wraps oneself in; “beauty is” praiseworthy traits that earned their possessors honor. “Al-hidthan”: the disliked vicissitudes of time that turn. “Al-sabigha”: the coat of mail, and he had a coat of mail of gold. “Al-'adda'”: the mare that runs much. “Al-'alanda” (with fatha): the thick, strong, swift one; and “shay' 'alad”: hard — “i'landa al-ba'ir”: became strong. “Al-nahd”: huge, tall. “Al-shutab” (with damma): the streaks of the sword. “Al-abdan”: the short coats of mail; and if it cuts the helmet and the body-armor, though both are of iron, it cuts others a fortiori. He praised himself with courage, then with patience, saying: many of my brothers I lowered into graves with my own hand, and despite that I did not grieve at all, neither little nor much, “in” being superfluous. “Al-hala'”: intensity of impatience. And in the hadith: “Of the worst of what a servant is given: a wailing stinginess and a heart-tearing cowardice,” i.e. he wails in it, and as if it tears out his heart. “Tazannada fulan”: he was narrowed in answering and became angry. “Al-muzannad”: a proverb for a thing. And of the despised it is said: “zandan fi marqa'a,” so “al-zand” is the paltry thing. And it is narrated: “Zaydan,” with ya', on the basis that it is Zayd ibn al-Khattab, brother of 'Umar ؓ who was a friend of his in the Jahiliyya. And it is narrated: “wa-hal yaruddu buka'i?” i.e. I did not grieve, because I knew that it does not benefit.
1. (1) . وإذا المنية أنشبت أظفارها
…. ألفيت كل تميمة لا تنفع وتجلدي للشامتين أريهم
…. أنى لريب الدهر لا أتضعضع لأبى ذؤيب خويلد بن خالد المخزومي، يرثى بنيه. روى أن معاوية مرض، فعاده الحسن بن على رضى الله عنهما فقال: كحلونى وألبسونى عمامتي، وأظهر القوة وأنشد له البيت الثاني، فأجابه الحسن بغتة بالأول. وشبه المنية بالسبع على طريق المكنية. وإنشاب الأظفار: تخييل. ومنى له: قدر له. والمنية: الموت لأنه مقدر. والانشاب: الغرز والتعليق. ألفيت: أى وجدت كل تميمة لا تنفع، وهي ما يعلق على الولدان خوف الجن والحسد. وتجلدي: أى تصبرى وتصلبي. مبتدأ. وأريهم: خبره، أى أظهر لهم به أنى لا أتضعضع وأتخشع وأضعف لأجل ريب الدهر، أى حدثانه الطارئ من حيث لا أشعر. [.....]
2. . ليس الجمال بمئزر
…. فاعلم وإن رديت برداً إن الجمال معادن
…. ومناقب أورثن مجداً أعددن للحدثان سا
…. بقة وعداء علندى نهداً وذا شطب يقد
…. البيض والأبدان قدا كم من أخ لي صالح
…. بوأته بيدي لحدا ما إن هلعت ولا جز
…. عت ولا يرد بكاى زندا لعمرو بن معد يكرب. يقول: ليس الجمال بفاخر الثياب. وفاعلم: اعتراض. والخطاب لغير معين، أى ليس كذلك وإن ألبستها والبرد، ثوب سابغ يرتدى به إن الجمال خصال حميدة أكسبت أصحابها الشرف. والحدثان: مكروه الدهر المنقلب. والسابغة الدرع، وكانت له درع من ذهب. والعداء: الفرس الكثير العدو. والعلندى- بالفتح-: الغليظ الشديد السريع. وشيء علند: صلب- واعلندى البعير: اشتد. والنهد: الضخم الطويل. والشطب- بالضم-: طرائق السيف. والأبدان: الدروع القصيرة، وإذا قطع البيضة والبدن مع أنهما من الحديد، قطع غيرهما بالأولى: مدح نفسه بالشجاعة، ثم بالصبر فقال: كثير من إخوانى أنزلتهم اللحود بيدي، ومع ذلك ما جزعت لا قليلا ولا كثيراً فان زائدة. والهلع: شدة الجزع. وفي الحديث «من شر ما أوتى العبد: شح هالع، وجبن خالع» أى يهلع فيه وكأنه يخلع فؤاده. وتزند فلان. ضاق بالجواب وغضب. والمزند: مثل في الشيء. ويقال للحقير: زندان في مرقعة، فالزند: الشيء الحقير. ويروى: زيدا: بالياء، على أنه زيد بن الخطاب أخو عمر رضى الله عنه، كان صديقا له في الجاهلية. ويروى: وهل يرد بكائي؟ أى: لم أجزع، لعلمي أنه لا ينفع.
Vol. 2, p. 526
1. (1) . His statement “because the unlawful is not provision” — this is according to the Mu'tazila. According to Ahl al-Sunna it is provision like the lawful. (ʿ)
2. Mahmud said: “What is meant by ‘of what We have provided them’ is the lawful, because the unlawful is not provision and is not attributed to God Almighty.” Ahmad said: The truth is that there is no provider but God — “Indeed God is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm” — just as there is no creator but God — “Is there any creator other than God?” So if reason and revelation both require that there be no provider but God, what statement remains after that for the Qadari who claims that most servants provide for themselves, because most is unlawful, while he is nevertheless set upon his corrupt belief, not leaving it, neither revelatory nor rational warnings restraining him nor deterring him? “So in what statement after God and His verses will they believe?”
3. Mahmud said: “What is meant is the outcome of this world and the destination of its people … etc.” Ahmad said: The unrestricted “outcome” has recurred, such as “and the disbelievers will know for whom is the outcome of the abode,” “for whom is the outcome of the abode,” and “the outcome is for the righteous,” and what is meant in all of that is the good outcome and happiness. Al-Zamakhshari deduces, from the recurrence of the unrestricted “outcome” while the good outcome is meant, that it is what God intended, and so it is the principle, and the other outcome, since it was not intended but incidental, contrary to what is intended and the principle, did not deserve to be expressed except with a qualification that makes it understood, as in His saying “and the outcome of the disbelievers is the Fire.” All of that on the part of al-Zamakhshari is a rushing to attribute to God an intention of what did not occur and a will of what was not, in collision with what God made the tongues of the bearers of the Law pronounce: what God wills is, and what He does not will is not. And there is nothing in the unrestricted occurrence of that to establish that it is the principle with respect to intention; its being the principle is with respect to command, and we say: that which leads to a praiseworthy outcome is commanded, and that which leads to a bad one is prohibited; hence the good outcome is the principle. And God is the Granter of success.
1. (1) . قوله «لأن الحرام لا يكون رزقا» هذا عند المعتزلة. أما عند أهل السنة فيكون رزقا كالحلال. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «المراد مما رزقناهم من الحلال، لأن الحرام لا يكون رزقا ولا يسند إلى الله تعالى» قال أحمد: الحق أن لا رازق إلا الله إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ كما أنه لا خالق إلا الله هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ فإذا اقتضى العقل والسمع جميعاً أن لا رازق إلا الله فأى مقال بعد ذلك يبقى للقدرى الزاعم أن أكثر العبيد يرزقون أنفسهم لأن الغالب الحرام وهو مع ذلك مصمم على معتقده الفاسد لا يدعه ولا تكفه القوارع السمعية والعقلية ولا تردعه فبأى حديث بعد الله وآياته يؤمنون.
3. . قال محمود: «المراد عاقبة الدنيا ومرجع أهلها
…. الخ» قال أحمد: قد تكرر مجيء العاقبة المطلقة مثل وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ، مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ عاقِبَةُ الدَّارِ. وَالْعاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ والمراد في جميع ذلك: عقبى الخير والسعادة، والزمخشري يستنبط من تكرار مجيء العاقبة المطلقة والمراد عاقبة الخير أنها هي التي أرادها الله فهي الأصل والعاقبة الأخرى لما لم تكن مرادة بل عارضة على خلاف المراد والأصل لم يكن من حقها أن يعبر عنها إلا بتقييد يفهمها كقوله وَعُقْبَى الْكافِرِينَ النَّارُ كل ذلك من الزمخشري تهالك على أن ينسب إلى الله إرادة ما لم يقع ومشيئة ما لم يكن مصادمة لما أنطق الله به ألسنة حملة الشريعة ما شاء الله كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن، وليس في مجيء ذلك على الإطلاق ما يعين أنه الأصل باعتبار الارادة، ففعله الأصل باعتبار الأمر، ونحن نقول: إن المؤدى إلى حمد العاقبة مأمور به، والمؤدى إلى سوئها منهى عنه، فمن ثم كانت عاقبة الخير هي الأصل، والله الموفق.
Vol. 2, p. 527
1. (1) . “I see the wild beasts grazing today in the courtyard of the sanctuary, in place of what I used to see there — plump maidens.” He says: I see wild animals grazing in the courtyard of the sanctuary at this time, in place of the beloved ones I used to see there; “qad ara” is the narration of a past state, and “qad” is to bring it near. “Al-awanis”: plural of anisa. “Al-budn”: plural of badina, i.e. plump of body.
2. 'Abd al-Razzaq and al-Tabari recorded it through the narration of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: “The Prophet ﷺ used to …” then he mentioned it — and added: “Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman used to do that.”
1. (1) . أرى الوحش ترعي اليوم في ساحة الحما
…. بما قد أرى فيها أوانس بدنا يقول: أرى الوحش ترعى في ساحة الحما في هذا الزمان، بدل ما كنت أرى فيها الأحبة، فقد أرى: حكاية حال ماضية، وقد لتقريبها. والأوانس: جمع آنسة. والبدن: جمع بادنة، أى سمينة البدن.
2. . أخرجه عبد الرزاق والطبري من رواية سهيل بن أبى صالح عن محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكره» وزاد «كان أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان يفعلون ذلك» .

Q 13:25 · Vol. 2, p. 527

Verse 25

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And those who break the covenant of God after its confirmation, and sever what God has ordered to be joined, and cause corruption on earth — those will have the curse, and they will have the evil abode (25)
وَالَّذِينَ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثاقِهِ وَيَقْطَعُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ أُولئِكَ لَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ وَلَهُمْ سُوءُ الدَّارِ (25)
Vol. 2, p. 527
“After its confirmation” — after what they confirmed by it, of admission and acceptance. “The evil abode”: it may mean the evil outcome of this world, because it is in contrast with “the best end of the abode”; and it may be that by “abode” is meant Hell, and by its evil its punishment.
مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثاقِهِ من بعد ما أوثقوه به من الاعتراف والقبول سُوءُ الدَّارِ يحتمل أن يراد سوء عاقبة الدنيا، لأنه في مقابلة عقبى الدار،. ويجوز أن يراد بالدار جهنم، وبسوئها عذابها.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 527
1. (1) . “I see the wild beasts grazing today in the courtyard of the sanctuary, in place of what I used to see there — plump maidens.” He says: I see wild animals grazing in the courtyard of the sanctuary at this time, in place of the beloved ones I used to see there; “qad ara” is the narration of a past state, and “qad” is to bring it near. “Al-awanis”: plural of anisa. “Al-budn”: plural of badina, i.e. plump of body.
2. 'Abd al-Razzaq and al-Tabari recorded it through the narration of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: “The Prophet ﷺ used to …” then he mentioned it — and added: “Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman used to do that.”
1. (1) . أرى الوحش ترعي اليوم في ساحة الحما
…. بما قد أرى فيها أوانس بدنا يقول: أرى الوحش ترعى في ساحة الحما في هذا الزمان، بدل ما كنت أرى فيها الأحبة، فقد أرى: حكاية حال ماضية، وقد لتقريبها. والأوانس: جمع آنسة. والبدن: جمع بادنة، أى سمينة البدن.
2. . أخرجه عبد الرزاق والطبري من رواية سهيل بن أبى صالح عن محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكره» وزاد «كان أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان يفعلون ذلك» .
19
Q 13:26 · Vol. 2, pp. 527–528

Verse 26

The verse as the commentary quotes it
God extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoiced in the worldly life, while the worldly life compared to the Hereafter is only a [brief] enjoyment (26)
اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلاَّ مَتاعٌ (26)
Vol. 2, p. 527
“God extends provision” — i.e. God alone extends provision and restricts it, none other; and it is He who extended
اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ أى الله وحده هو يبسط الرزق ويقدره دون غيره، وهو الذي بسط
Vol. 2, p. 528
the provision of the people of Mecca and made it ample for them; “and they rejoiced” in what He extended to them of the world with the rejoicing of arrogance and exuberance, not the rejoicing of delight in God's bounty and favor to them, and they did not meet it with gratitude so as to deserve the bliss of the Hereafter; and it was hidden from them that the bliss of this world, beside the bliss of the Hereafter, is nothing but a paltry thing enjoyed like the hasty bite of a rider, i.e. what he hurries to eat of a few dates or a drink of sawiq or the like.
رزق أهل مكة ووسعه عليهم وَفَرِحُوا بما بسط لهم من الدنيا فرح بطر وأشر لا فرح سرور بفضل الله وإنعامه عليهم، ولم يقابلوه بالشكر حتى يستوجبوا نعيم الآخرة، وخفى عليهم أن نعيم الدنيا في جنب نعيم الآخرة ليس إلا شيئاً نزرا يتمتع به كعجالة الراكب، وهو ما يتعجله من تميرات أو شربة سويق أو نحو ذلك.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 527
1. (1) . “I see the wild beasts grazing today in the courtyard of the sanctuary, in place of what I used to see there — plump maidens.” He says: I see wild animals grazing in the courtyard of the sanctuary at this time, in place of the beloved ones I used to see there; “qad ara” is the narration of a past state, and “qad” is to bring it near. “Al-awanis”: plural of anisa. “Al-budn”: plural of badina, i.e. plump of body.
2. 'Abd al-Razzaq and al-Tabari recorded it through the narration of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: “The Prophet ﷺ used to …” then he mentioned it — and added: “Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman used to do that.”
1. (1) . أرى الوحش ترعي اليوم في ساحة الحما
…. بما قد أرى فيها أوانس بدنا يقول: أرى الوحش ترعى في ساحة الحما في هذا الزمان، بدل ما كنت أرى فيها الأحبة، فقد أرى: حكاية حال ماضية، وقد لتقريبها. والأوانس: جمع آنسة. والبدن: جمع بادنة، أى سمينة البدن.
2. . أخرجه عبد الرزاق والطبري من رواية سهيل بن أبى صالح عن محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي قال «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكره» وزاد «كان أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان يفعلون ذلك» .
20
Q 13:27–29 · Vol. 2, pp. 528–529

Verses 27 to 29

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And those who disbelieve say: Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord? Say: Indeed God leads astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back (27) Those who believed and whose hearts find peace in the remembrance of God. Unquestionably, in the remembrance of God hearts find peace (28) Those who believed and did righteous deeds — blessedness (tuba) is theirs, and a good place of return (29)
وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ قُلْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنابَ (27) الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أَلا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ (28) الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ طُوبى لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ (29)
Vol. 2, p. 528
Question
If you ask: how does their saying “Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord” fit His saying “Say: Indeed God leads astray whom He wills”?
فإن قلت: كيف طابق قولهم لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ قوله قُلْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ؟
Answer
I say: it is speech that runs the course of astonishment at their saying; for the dazzling, numerous signs given to the Messenger of God ﷺ were not given to any prophet before him, and the Qur'an alone suffices as a sign beyond every sign; so if they deny it and do not count it and make it as though no sign were ever sent down to him, that is a place for astonishment and disapproval. So it is as if it were said to them: How great is your obstinacy and how intense your determination on your disbelief: God leads astray whom He wills of those of your description of determination and hardness of resolve in disbelief, so there is no path to their guidance even if every sign were sent down; “and guides to Himself” whoever is contrary to your description — “turned back”: approached the truth; and its reality is that he entered into the turn of good. And “those who believed” is a substitute for “whoever turned back.” “And their hearts find peace in the remembrance of God” — in the remembrance of His mercy and forgiveness after anxiety and agitation from fear of Him, as in His saying “then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of God”; or they find peace in the mention of His proofs that indicate His oneness; or they find peace in the Qur'an, because it is a clear miracle that calms hearts and establishes certainty in them. “Those who believed” is a subject, and “tuba is theirs” is its predicate. It is also possible that it is a substitute for “the hearts,” on the assumption of an omitted annexed noun, i.e.: the hearts, the hearts of those who believed, find peace; and “tuba” is a verbal noun from taba, like busra and zulfa. The meaning of “tuba lak” is: you have gained goodness and pleasantness; and its position is accusative or nominative, like your saying “tayyiban lak” and “tayyibun lak,” “salaman lak” and “salamun lak.” And the reading in His saying “wa husnu ma'ab” with nominative and accusative shows you their positions. And the lam in “lahum” is for explanation, like that in “suqya lak”; and the waw in “tuba” is converted from ya' because of the damma before it, like muqin and musir. Makuza the bedouin read: tiba lahum, putting kasra on the ta' so that the ya' remains sound, as it is said: bid and ma'isha.
قلت: هو كلام يجرى مجرى التعجب من قولهم، وذلك أن الآيات الباهرة المتكاثرة التي أوتيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يؤتها نبىّ قبله، وكفى بالقرآن وحده آية وراء كل آية، فإذا جحدوها ولم يعتدّوا بها وجعلوه كأن آية لم تنزل عليه فط، كان موضعاً للتعجب والاستنكار، فكأنه قيل لهم: ما أعظم عنادكم وما أشد تصميمكم على كفركم: إن الله يضل من يشاء ممن كان على صفتكم من التصميم وشدّة الشكيمة في الكفر، فلا سبيل إلى اهتدائهم وإن أنزلت كل آية وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ كان على خلاف صفتكم أَنابَ أقبل إلى الحق، وحقيقته دخل في نوبة الخير، والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بدل من مَنْ أَنابَ. وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ بذكر رحمته ومغفرته بعد القلق والاضطراب من خشيته، كقوله ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أو تطمئن بذكر دلائله الدالة على وحدانيته، أو تطمئن بالقرآن لأنه معجزة بينة تسكن القلوب وتثبت اليقين فيها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مبتدأ، وطُوبى لَهُمْ خبره. ويجوز أن يكون بدلا من القلوب، على تقدير حذف المضاف، أى: تطمئن القلوب قلوب الذين آمنوا، وطوبى مصدر من طاب، كبشرى وزلفى. ومعنى «طوبى لك» أصبت خيراً وطيبا، ومحلها النصب أو الرفع، كقولك: طيبا لك، وطيب لك، وسلاما لك، وسلام لك. والقراءة في قوله وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ بالرفع والنصب، تدلك على محليها. واللام في لَهُمْ للبيان مثلها في سقيا لك، والواو في طوبى منقلبة عن ياء لضمة ما قبلها، كموقن وموسر. وقرأ مكوزة الأعرابى: طيبي لهم، فكسر الطاء لتسلم الياء، كما قيل: بيض ومعيشة.
Vol. 2, p. 529
21
Q 13:30 · Vol. 2, p. 529

Verse 30

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Thus have We sent you among a community before which [other] communities have passed on, that you may recite to them that which We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: He is my Lord; there is no god but Him; upon Him I rely, and to Him is my repentance (30)
كَذلِكَ أَرْسَلْناكَ فِي أُمَّةٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِها أُمَمٌ لِتَتْلُوَا عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِالرَّحْمنِ قُلْ هُوَ رَبِّي لا إِلهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ مَتابِ (30)
Vol. 2, p. 529
“Thus We sent you” — like that sending We sent you, meaning: We sent you with a sending that has status and excellence over all other sendings; then He explained how He sent him, saying “among a community before which communities have passed on,” i.e. We sent you among a community that many communities preceded, so it is the last of the communities and you are the seal of the prophets; “that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you” — that you may read to them the great Book that We revealed to you; “and they disbelieve” — and the state of these is that they disbelieve “in the Most Merciful” — in the One of utmost mercy, whose mercy encompasses everything, and whatever blessing they have is from Him, yet they disbelieved His favor in sending the like of you to them and in sending down upon them this inimitable Qur'an confirming the other Books. “Say: He is my Lord” — the One, exalted above partners; “upon Him I rely” — for my victory over you; “and to Him is my repentance” — so He will reward me for my steadfastness and striving against you.
كَذلِكَ أَرْسَلْناكَ مثل ذلك الإرسال أرسلناك، يعنى: أرسلناك إرسالا له شأن وفضل على سائر الإرسالات، ثم فسر كيف أرسله فقال فِي أُمَّةٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِها أُمَمٌ أى أرسلناك في أمة قد تقدمتها أمم كثيرة فهي آخر الأمم وأنت خاتم الأنبياء لِتَتْلُوَا عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ لتقرأ عليهم الكتاب العظيم الذي أوحينا إليك وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ وحال هؤلاء أنهم يكافرون بِالرَّحْمنِ بالبليغ الرحمة الذي وسعت رحمته كل شيء، وما بهم من نعمة فمنه، فكفروا بنعمته في إرسال مثلك إليهم وإنزال هذا القرآن المعجز المصدق لسائر الكتب عليهم قُلْ هُوَ رَبِّي الواحد المتعالي عن الشركاء عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ في نصرتي عليكم وَإِلَيْهِ مَتابِ فيثيبني على مصابرتكم ومجاهدتكم.
22
Q 13:31 · Vol. 2, pp. 529–531

Verse 31

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains were moved, or the earth were cut apart, or the dead were spoken to... Rather, to God belongs the matter entirely. Have those who believed not yet realized that if God willed, He could have guided all of mankind? And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck, for what they have done, by calamity, or it will settle near their home, until the promise of God comes. Indeed, God does not fail in His promise (31)
وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتى بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لَهَدَى النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً وَلا يَزالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا تُصِيبُهُمْ بِما صَنَعُوا قارِعَةٌ أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيباً مِنْ دارِهِمْ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعادَ (31)
Vol. 2, p. 529
“And if there were a Qur'an” — its answer is omitted, as you say to your servant “If I were to rise to you,” and leave out the answer. The meaning: and if there were a Qur'an by which mountains were moved from their places and shaken from their beds, “or the earth were cut apart” until it splits and separates into pieces, “or the dead were spoken to” so they hear and answer — it would be this Qur'an, for being the utmost in admonition and the end in warning and frightening, as He said: “Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split apart from fear of God.” This supports what I explained of His saying “that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you” — the intention of magnifying what was revealed to the Messenger of God ﷺ of the Qur'an. It is also said: its meaning: if there were a Qur'an by which the moving of mountains, the cutting of the earth, and the speaking to the dead and waking them took place, they would not believe in it and would not be awakened by it, as in His saying “And even if We had sent down to them the angels …” the verse. It is also said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: Move the mountains away from Mecca with your Qur'an so that it widens for us and we make gardens and estates in it,
وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً جوابه محذوف، كما تقول لغلامك: لو أنى قمت إليك، وتترك الجواب والمعنى: ولو أن قرآنا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ عن مقارّها، وزعزعت عن مضاجعها أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ حتى تتصدع وتتزايل قطعاً أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتى فتسمع وتجيب، لكان هذا القرآن لكونه غاية في التذكير ونهاية في الإنذار والتخويف، كما قال لَوْ أَنْزَلْنا هذَا الْقُرْآنَ عَلى جَبَلٍ لَرَأَيْتَهُ خاشِعاً مُتَصَدِّعاً مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ هذا يعضد ما فسرت به قوله لِتَتْلُوَا عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ من إرادة تعظيم ما أوحى إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن. وقيل: معناه ولو أن قرآنا وقع به تسيير الجبال وتقطيع الأرض وتكليم الموتى وتنبيههم، لما آمنوا به ولما تنبهوا عليه كقوله وَلَوْ أَنَّنا نَزَّلْنا إِلَيْهِمُ الْمَلائِكَةَ الآية. وقيل: إن أبا جهل بن هشام قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: سير بقرآنك الجبال عن مكة حتى تتسع لنا فنتخذ فيها البساتين والقطائع،
Vol. 2, p. 530
as they were subjected to David ﷺ if you are a prophet as you claim — for you are no lesser with God than David. And subject the wind for us by it so that we ride it and trade to Syria and return the same day, for crossing the long distance is hard on us — as the wind was subjected to Solomon ﷺ. Or raise for us by it two or three men or the dead among our forefathers: among them Qusayy ibn Kilab (1). So it was revealed. The meaning of “cutting the earth” on this account is: traversing it by travel and crossing it. From al-Farra': it is connected with what is before it. The meaning: “and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful … and if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved,” with what is between them parenthetical; and it is not far from correctness. It is also said: “the earth were cut apart” — split open and made into rivers and springs. “Rather, to God belongs the matter entirely” in two senses: one: rather to God belongs power over everything, and He is able to do the signs they proposed, except that His knowledge that showing them is corruption turns Him away. The second: rather it belongs to God to compel them to belief, and He is able to compel, except that He built the matter of obligation upon choice. It is supported by His saying “Have those who believed not yet despaired that if God willed” — meaning the will of compulsion and coercion (2) — “He would have guided all people.” And the meaning of “a-fa-lam yay'as” is “a-fa-lam ya'lam” (have they not known). It is said: it is a dialect of a people of al-Nakha'. It is also said: despair was used in the sense of knowledge only because it implies it, since the one who despairs of something knows it will not be; just as hope is used in the sense of fear, and forgetting in the sense of leaving, because of implication. Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Riyahi said: “I said to them in the mountain pass as they gambled over me: Have you not yet known that I am the son of the horseman Zahdam? (3)” And evidence for it is that Ali, Ibn Abbas, and a group of the Companions and Followers read: a-fa-lam yatabayyan, which is an explanation of a-fa-lam yay'as. It is also said: the scribe wrote it while drowsy, with the strokes of the sins levelled; and this and the like is among what is not to be believed
كما سخرت لداود عليه السلام إن كنت نبياً كما تزعم، فلست بأهون على الله من داود. وسخر لنا به الريح لنركبها ونتجر إلى الشام ثم نرجع في يومنا، فقد شق علينا قطع المسافة البعيدة كما سخرت لسليمان عليه السلام. أو ابعث لنا به رجلين أو ثلاثة ممن مات من آبائنا: منهم قصى بن كلاب «1» فنزلت. ومعنى تقطيع الأرض على هذا: قطعها بالسير ومجاوزتها. وعن الفراء: هو متعلق بما قبله. والمعنى: وهم يكافرون بالرحمن وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ وما بينهما اعتراض، وليس ببعيد من السداد. وقيل قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ شققت فجعلت أنهارا وعيونا بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً على معنيين، أحدهما: بل لله القدرة على كل شيء، وهو قادر على الآيات التي اقترحوها، إلا أنّ علمه بأنّ إظهارها مفسدة يصرفه. والثاني: بل لله أن يلجئهم إلى الإيمان، وهو قادر على الإلجاء لولا أنه بنى أمر التكليف على الاختيار. ويعضده قوله أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ يعنى مشيئة الإلجاء والقسر «2» لَهَدَى النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً ومعنى أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ أفلم يعلم. قيل: هي لغة قوم من النخع. وقيل: إنما استعمل اليأس بمعنى العلم لتضمنه معناه، لأنّ اليائس عن الشيء عالم بأنه لا يكون، كما استعمل الرجاء في معنى الخوف، والنسيان في معنى الترك لتضمن ذلك. قال سحيم بن وثيل الرياحي: أَقُولُ لَهُمْ بِالشِّعْبِ إذْ يَيْسِرُونَنِى … أَلَمْ تَيْأَسُوا أنِّى ابْنُ فَارِسِ زَهْدَمِ «3» ويدل عليه أن علياً وابن عباس وجماعة من الصحابة والتابعين قرءوا: أفلم يتبين، وهو تفسير أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ وقيل: إنما كتبه الكاتب وهو ناعس مستوى السينات، وهذا ونحوه مما لا يصدق
Vol. 2, p. 531
in the Book of God, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it; and how could such a thing be hidden so that it remains fixed between the two covers of the Imam [codex]? And it was being turned over in the hands of those notable men, careful about God's religion, its guardians, who were not heedless of its great or fine matters, especially of the canon to which recourse is made and the foundation upon which the structure stands. And this, by God, is a fabrication in which there is no doubt. It is also possible that “an law yasha'u” is connected to “amanu,” in the sense: Have those who believed not despaired of the faith of these disbelievers, [knowing] that if God willed He would have guided all people, and would have guided them? “will keep striking them for what they did” of their disbelief and evil deeds — “qari'a,” a disaster that strikes them with what God inflicts on them at every time of kinds of afflictions and misfortunes in their persons, their children and their wealth; “or it will settle,” the calamity, “near them,” so they are terrified and agitated, and its sparks fly toward them and its evils extend to them; “until the promise of God comes,” which is their death, or the Resurrection. And it is said: the disbelievers of Mecca will not cease to be struck, for what they did to the Messenger of God ﷺ of enmity and denial, by a calamity, because the Messenger of God ﷺ did not cease to dispatch expeditions (1), which raided around Mecca and snatched from them and seized some of their livestock. Or you, O Muhammad, will settle near their abode with your army, as you settled at al-Hudaybiyya, until the promise of God comes — which is the conquest of Mecca — and God had promised him that.
في كتاب الله الذي لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه، وكيف يخفى مثل هذا حتى يبقى ثابتا بين دفتي الإمام. وكان متقلبا في أيدى أولئك الأعلام المحتاطين في دين الله المهيمنين عليه لا يغفلون عن جلائله ودقائقه، خصوصا عن القانون الذي إليه المرجع، والقاعدة التي عليها البناء، وهذه والله فرية ما فيها مرية. ويجوز أن يتعلق أَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ بآمنوا، على: أولم يقنط عن إيمان هؤلاء الكفرة الذين آمنوا بأن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا ولهداهم تُصِيبُهُمْ بِما صَنَعُوا من كفرهم وسوء أعمالهم قارِعَةٌ داهية تقرعهم بما يحل الله بهم في كل وقت من صنوف البلايا والمصائب في نفوسهم وأولادهم وأموالهم أَوْ تَحُلُّ القارعة قَرِيباً منهم فيفزعون ويضطربون ويتطاير إليهم شرارها، ويتعدى إليهم شرورها حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ اللَّهِ وهو موتهم، أو القيامة. وقيل: ولا يزال كفار مكة تصيبهم بما صنعوا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من العداوة والتكذيب قارعة، لأنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان لا يزال يبعث السرايا «1» فتغير حول مكة وتختطف منهم، وتصيب من مواشيهم. أو تحل أنت يا محمد قريبا من دارهم بجيشك، كما حل بالحديبية، حتى يأتى وعد الله وهو فتح مكة، وكان الله قد وعده ذلك
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 530
1. (1) . I did not find it in this form. Ibn Rabi'a narrated from Abu Usama from Mujalid from al-Sha'bi, who said: Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ: “If you are a prophet as you claim, then push apart the two mountains of Mecca — I think it was these two, a distance of four or five days — so that we may sow in it and graze, and raise for us our forefathers from the dead so that they speak to us and inform us that you are a prophet, or carry us to Syria, or to Yemen, or to al-Hira, so that we go and come in one night as you claimed you did.” So God Almighty revealed “And if there were a Qur'an …” the verse. And Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through 'Atiyya ibn Abi Sa'id, who said: they said to Muhammad ﷺ: “If you would move the mountains of Mecca for us so that it widens and we plough in it, or cut the earth for us as Solomon used to cut it by the wind for his people.” And Abu Ya'la narrated from the hadith of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, who said: “When ‘And warn your closest kinsmen’ was revealed, the Messenger of God ﷺ cried out: O family of Quraysh! So Quraysh came to him. He cautioned and warned them, and they said: You claim that you are a prophet, and that the wind and the mountains were subjected to Solomon, and that the sea was subjected to Moses, and that Jesus used to give life to the dead. So pray to God to move these mountains away from us and make the earth gush rivers for us, so we make them plowlands and sow and eat; or pray to God to give life to our dead so we speak to them and they speak to us; or pray to God to turn this rock beside you into gold so we may carve from it and be enriched. He said: While we were around him, revelation came down upon him. When it was lifted from him, he said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, He has given me what you asked, and had I wished it, it would have been, but He informed me that if He gave you that and then you disbelieved, He would punish you. So it was revealed.”
2. His statement “if God willed — i.e. the will of compulsion” — this is according to the Mu'tazila, not Ahl al-Sunna. (ʿ)
3. The explanation of this line occurred in Volume One, page 261; consult it if you wish. End. (the corrector)
1. (1) . لم أجده بهذا السياق، وقد روى ابن ربيعة عن أبى أسامة عن مجالد عن الشعبي قال قالت قريش النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «إن كنت نبياً كما تزعم فباعد بين جبلي مكة- أحسبها هذين مسيرة أربعة أيام أو خمسة حتى تزرع فيها ونرعى، وابعث لنا آباءنا من الموتى حتى يكلمونا ويخبرون أنك نبى، أو احملنا إلى الشام، أو إلى اليمن، أو إلى الحيرة، حتى نذهب ونجيء في ليلة كما زعمت أنك فعلت. فأنزل الله تعالى وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً- الآية وروى ابن أبى حاتم وابن مردويه من طريق عطية بن أبى سعيد قال قالوا لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لو سيرت لنا جبال مكة حتى تتسع فنحرث فيها، أو قطعت لنا الأرض كما كان سليمان يقطع لقومه الريح» وروى أبو يعلى من حديث الزبير بن العوام يقول «لما نزلت: وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين صاح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا آل قريش، فجاءته قريش. فحذرهم وأنذرهم فقالوا: تزعم أنك نبى وأن سليمان سخر له الريح والجبال، وأن موسى سخر له البحر، وأن عيسى كان يحيى الموتى. فادع الله أن يسير عنا هذه الجبال وتنفجر لنا الأرض أنهارا فنتخذها محارث فنزرع ونأكل أو ادع الله أن يحيى لنا موتانا فنكلمهم ويكلمونا أو ادع الله أن يصبر هذه الصخرة التي بجنبك ذهبا فننحت منها ويغنينا قال: فبينما نحن حوله إذ نزل عليه الوحى. فلما سرى عنه قال: والذي نفسي بيده، لقد أعطانى ما سألتم ولو شئت كان ولكن أخبرنى أنه إن أعطاكم ذلك ثم كفرتم يعذبكم. فنزلت» .
2. . قوله «أن لو يشاء الله يعنى مشيئة الإلجاء» هذا عند المعتزلة دون أهل السنة. (ع)

Q 13:32 · Vol. 2, p. 531

Verse 32

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And messengers before you were indeed mocked, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, so how was My punishment (32)
وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كانَ عِقابِ (32)
Vol. 2, p. 531
“Al-imla'”: respite, and that one be left a span of time in ease and security, like the beast that is given slack in the pasture; and this is a threat to them and an answer to their proposing signs to the Messenger of God ﷺ in mockery of him, and a consolation to him.
الإملاء: الإمهال، وأن يترك ملاوة من الزمان في خفض وأمن، كالبهيمة يملى لها في المرعى وهذا وعيد لهم وجواب عن اقتراحهم الآيات على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. استهزاء به وتسلية له.
